words.definitionEn: A basic food eaten regularly and in large amounts in a particular place.
words.example: Rice is a staple food in many households.

words.definitionEn: Regularly receive less food than the body needs over a long period.
words.example: Families with very low incomes may be chronically underfed.

words.definitionEn: The problem of people around the world not having enough food.
words.example: Better access to affordable food is essential for tackling world hunger.

words.definitionEn: A situation in which there is not enough food available.
words.example: The drought caused a scarcity of food in nearby villages.

words.definitionEn: The buying and selling of food between places or countries.
words.example: Food trade allows the country to import rice when local harvests fail.

words.definitionEn: Farmers who mainly produce food for themselves and their families.
words.translationUz: o‘z ehtiyoji uchun mahsulot yetishtiruvchi dehqonlar
words.example: Many subsistence farmers sell only what their families do not need.

words.definitionEn: Produce crops that people can eat.
words.example: We grow food in a small garden behind our house.

words.definitionEn: Keep food for later use under suitable conditions.
words.example: The village needs better facilities to store food after the harvest.

words.definitionEn: Crop varieties whose genetic material has been changed using genetic engineering; often called genetically modified varieties.
words.translationUz: genetik muhandislik yordamida yaratilgan oziq-ovqat navlari
words.example: Researchers are studying genetically engineered varieties of food that can tolerate drought.

words.definitionEn: Maize developed or selected to grow well or produce high yields under particular conditions; not necessarily genetically modified.
words.example: The farmers tested high-performance maize on a small part of their land.

words.definitionEn: Strength, energy or healthy growth; vigor is American spelling and vigour is British.
words.example: The young plants showed remarkable vigour after the rain.

words.definitionEn: The part of a plant from which a new plant can grow.
words.example: She planted each seed in moist soil.

words.definitionEn: Increase the amount, strength or activity of something.
words.example: Some growers want to intensify food production on their existing land.

words.definitionEn: Producing crops or raising animals mainly to sell them for profit.
words.example: Commercial farming supplies vegetables to supermarkets across the region.

words.definitionEn: The total greenhouse gas emissions associated with a person, activity or product.
words.translationUz: uglerod izi; issiqxona gazlari chiqindilari miqdori
words.example: The company is measuring the carbon footprint of its food deliveries.

words.definitionEn: A tall tropical plant whose stems are used to produce sugar.
words.example: Farmers grow sugar cane in the warmer parts of the country.

words.definitionEn: A root crop grown to produce sugar.
words.example: This factory processes sugar beet from nearby farms.

words.definitionEn: Transport vegetables by truck; especially American usage.
words.example: Suppliers truck vegetables from rural farms to city markets.

words.definitionEn: Glass or plastic growing structures warmed by a heating system.
words.example: The tomatoes are grown in heated greenhouses during winter.

words.definitionEn: In this topic, the stages food passes through from production to consumption; also an ecological feeding relationship.
words.example: Temperature control matters at every stage of the food chain.

words.definitionEn: Reduce the carbon emissions associated with fuel; decarbonize transport or switch to lower-carbon fuels is often more natural.
words.translationUz: yoqilg‘i bilan bog‘liq uglerod chiqindilarini kamaytirmoq
words.example: To decarbonize transport, the supplier is switching some delivery vans to electricity.

words.definitionEn: Unexpected in a way that contrasts with what someone would normally expect.
words.example: It is ironic that the town exports fruit while some local families cannot afford it.

words.definitionEn: Become more able to meet your own needs without relying on outside supplies.
words.example: The community hopes to increase self-sufficiency by growing more vegetables.

words.definitionEn: The preparation and use of land for growing crops.
words.example: The land has been under cultivation for several generations.

words.definitionEn: Growing crops using methods established over generations in a community.
words.example: Traditional cropping in this village includes growing several crops together.

words.definitionEn: Cut down trees.
words.example: Some farmers fell trees to create more space for crops.

words.definitionEn: Cut back a tree's upper branches to encourage new growth at the top.
words.example: Workers pollard the trees to manage their size and collect branches.

words.definitionEn: Grow again or restore something to a healthy condition.
words.example: The project gives damaged woodland time to regenerate.

words.definitionEn: A grain crop such as wheat or maize; also a breakfast food made from processed grains.
words.translationUz: donli ekin; don mahsulotidan tayyorlangan nonushta
words.example: Millet is a cereal that farmers grow in this area.

words.definitionEn: A group of cereal crops with small grains used as food or animal feed.
words.example: The family uses millet to make porridge.

words.definitionEn: A sweet-tasting edible root, often with orange, white or purple flesh.
words.example: We roasted a sweet potato for lunch.

words.definitionEn: An edible seed that develops underground in a pod; groundnut is another name for peanut.
words.example: The farmer sells groundnuts at the local market.

words.definitionEn: Edible seeds or pods of several plants, often used as a source of protein.
words.example: She added beans to the vegetable stew.

words.definitionEn: Vegetables whose leaves are eaten, such as spinach and lettuce.
words.example: The garden provides leafy vegetables for the family.

words.definitionEn: Collecting crops when they are ready to be used.
words.example: Harvesting begins once the grain is ripe.

words.definitionEn: Removing unwanted plants from a growing area.
words.example: Regular weeding gives the young crops more space to grow.

words.definitionEn: Substances that living things need for growth and health.
words.example: Plants absorb nutrients from the soil.

words.definitionEn: Crops that complete their life cycle within one growing season.
words.example: Many annual crops must be planted again each year.

words.definitionEn: Soil that has lost much of its fertility, often through repeated cropping without replacement of nutrients.
words.example: The farmer added organic matter to improve the exhausted soil.

words.definitionEn: The upper level of groundwater in the ground.
words.example: The water table fell during the long dry season.

words.definitionEn: A farming system that combines trees with crops or livestock on the same land.
words.translationUz: daraxtlar bilan ekin yoki chorvani birga yetishtirish tizimi
words.example: Agroforestry allows the family to grow fruit trees alongside food crops.

words.definitionEn: Supply water to land or crops artificially.
words.example: Farmers use water from the reservoir to irrigate their fields.

words.definitionEn: Fishing that takes place throughout the year, rather than only in one season.
words.example: The report examines whether year-round fishing is possible on the lake.

words.definitionEn: A fish often eaten for its pink or orange flesh; many salmon migrate between rivers and the sea.
words.example: We ordered grilled salmon with vegetables.

words.definitionEn: The care and management of crops during their growth.
words.example: Good crop husbandry includes timely planting and weeding.

words.definitionEn: A farmer who produces beans or maize.
words.example: The maize grower bought new equipment for harvesting.

words.definitionEn: The activity of animals eating grass or other low-growing plants.
words.example: The cattle spend most of the day grazing.

words.definitionEn: Turn over and loosen soil with a plough before planting; plow is American spelling.
words.example: The farmer will plough the land before sowing wheat.

words.definitionEn: Chickens that can move around freely; free-roaming chickens is a more natural expression.
words.example: Free-roaming chickens searched for food around the yard.

words.definitionEn: Kill chickens or goats for meat.
words.translationUz: go‘sht uchun tovuq yoki echki so‘ymoq
words.example: The farm sends its goats to a licensed facility to be slaughtered.

words.definitionEn: Soil from which water has washed away soluble substances, including some nutrients.
words.example: Heavy rainfall can leave farmers with leached soil.

words.definitionEn: Areas, industries or activities concerned with catching or raising fish commercially.
words.example: Local fisheries provide jobs as well as food.

words.definitionEn: Encourage people to buy or support food produced under organic farming standards.
words.example: The campaign aims to promote organic food in local shops.

words.definitionEn: A broad expression for farming that relies on natural processes; not a precise certification term.
words.example: The grower describes composting as one of her natural farming methods.

words.definitionEn: A substance used to control pests, such as insects, weeds or fungi.
words.example: The farmer checked whether the pesticide was approved for that crop.

words.definitionEn: Choose to eat organically produced food; a common informal expression.
words.example: She tries to eat organic when suitable products fit her budget.

words.definitionEn: A mocking expression for large numbers of people who eat lots of junk food; avoid it in neutral writing.
words.translationUz: tez tayyor ovqatni ko‘p yeydigan ommani masxaralovchi ibora
words.example: The writer calls customers the “junk-food scoffing masses,” which makes the article sound judgmental.

words.definitionEn: Widely used farming methods that are not restricted to organic standards.
words.example: The report compares conventional farming with organic farming.

words.definitionEn: Manufactured substances added to soil or crops to supply nutrients; synthetic fertilizers is a more precise term.
words.example: The farm uses man-made fertilizers to replace nutrients removed by crops.

words.definitionEn: Growing different crops on the same land in a planned sequence.
words.example: The farmer uses crop rotation instead of planting wheat every season.

words.definitionEn: Farmers who follow organic production standards, which restrict many synthetic inputs.
words.example: Organic farmers may use crop rotation and compost to manage soil fertility.

words.definitionEn: The activities involved in producing food, including farming and processing.
words.example: Water shortages can make food production more difficult.

words.definitionEn: Move food from one place to another.
words.example: Refrigerated vehicles transport food to the supermarkets.

words.definitionEn: Providing useful nutrients that the body needs.
words.example: Lentil soup can be a nutritious and affordable meal.

words.definitionEn: How foods contribute to health; nutritional value is often the more precise expression.
words.example: The lesson explores the health value of foods we eat regularly.

words.definitionEn: Add animal waste to the soil to supply nutrients and organic matter.
words.example: The growers fertilize their fields with manure before planting.

words.term: Organic or non-organic system of production
words.definitionEn: A way of producing food that either follows organic standards or does not.
words.translationUz: organik yoki noorganik ishlab chiqarish tizimi
words.example: The study compares an organic system of production with a non-organic one.

words.definitionEn: Poisonous substances produced by living organisms; sometimes used more loosely for harmful substances.
words.translationUz: tirik organizmlar ishlab chiqaradigan zaharli moddalar
words.example: Some moulds can produce toxins in food.

words.definitionEn: Brown bread using dry heat.
words.example: I usually toast bread for breakfast.

words.definitionEn: Use selective breeding over generations to reduce or remove undesirable inherited characteristics.
words.translationUz: seleksiya orqali zararli irsiy xususiyatlarni kamaytirmoq
words.example: Plant breeders hope to breed out harmful traits from the variety.

words.definitionEn: Substances added to food for a purpose, such as preservation, colour, flavour or texture.
words.example: The label lists the additives used in the sauce.

words.definitionEn: Genetically modified crops, whose genetic material has been altered using genetic engineering.
words.example: The class discussed arguments for and against growing GM crops.

words.definitionEn: A figurative description of Europe's neatly maintained landscapes; a broad rhetorical generalization, not a technical term.
words.example: The article contrasts “well-manicured Europe” with areas where farming conditions are harsher.

words.definitionEn: The amounts of crops or other products obtained from a farm or area.
words.example: The farmers hope better irrigation will increase their yields.

words.definitionEn: A figurative expression for land lacking nutrients or other resources needed for growth.
words.example: After years without replenishment, the starved land produced very little.

words.definitionEn: Practical methods used to grow crops or raise animals.
words.example: Students compared traditional and modern farming techniques.

words.definitionEn: Details about a food's energy content and nutrients, usually shown on its label.
words.example: I checked the nutritional information before choosing a cereal.

words.definitionEn: A cupboard or small room used to store food and kitchen supplies.
words.example: Our kitchen pantry contains rice, beans and dried herbs.

words.definitionEn: One of the foods or substances used to make a dish or product.
words.example: Tomato is the main ingredient in this sauce.

words.definitionEn: Organizations that monitor health-related issues and raise concerns; a journalistic expression.
words.example: Health watchdogs called for clearer information on food packaging.

words.definitionEn: A person who studies or advises on nutrition; qualifications and title regulation vary by country.
words.example: The school invited a nutritionist to discuss food choices.

words.definitionEn: A waxy, fat-like substance made by the body and found in animal-derived foods.
words.example: The article explains the difference between cholesterol in food and cholesterol in the blood.

words.definitionEn: Foods or other products obtained from animals; animal-source foods is common in nutrition contexts.
words.example: Eggs and milk are animal-sourced products.

words.definitionEn: The yellow or orange central part of an egg.
words.example: Whisk the egg yolk into the sauce.

words.definitionEn: Meat from cattle.
words.example: He ordered beef with rice and vegetables.

words.definitionEn: Birds raised for meat or eggs, or their meat, such as chicken and turkey.
words.example: The shop sells fresh poultry and fish.

words.definitionEn: A small shellfish commonly eaten as seafood.
words.example: She added shrimp to the noodles.

words.definitionEn: Meat from pigs.
words.example: This dish contains pork, so it is unsuitable for some diners.

words.definitionEn: Oil obtained from cotton seeds and used in some foods.
words.example: Cottonseed oil appears in the product's ingredient list.

words.definitionEn: Rendered fat from cattle, used in cooking and other products.
words.example: The traditional recipe uses beef tallow for frying.

words.definitionEn: Oil obtained from plants and used in cooking or food production.
words.example: Heat a little vegetable oil in the pan.

words.definitionEn: A noticeable, usually pleasant smell, especially from food or drink.
words.example: The aroma of fresh bread filled the kitchen.

words.definitionEn: Having little flavour or excitement; usually mildly negative when describing food.
words.example: The soup was bland until we added herbs.

words.definitionEn: Substances added to slow spoilage and help food remain usable for longer.
words.example: The packaging states that no preservatives have been added.

words.definitionEn: Vegetable oil extracted from soybeans.
words.example: The dressing is made with soybean oil.

words.definitionEn: One part of a larger mixture, system or product.
words.example: Oil is an important component of this dressing.

words.definitionEn: Become part of what someone eats; enter someone's diet is more natural.
words.example: Ready-made meals entered his diet when he started working longer hours.

words.definitionEn: Foods changed from their original state through methods such as cooking, freezing, canning or drying.
words.example: Canned beans and frozen vegetables are examples of processed foods.

words.definitionEn: Put food into boxes for storage or sale.
words.example: Workers box the biscuits before they are shipped.

words.definitionEn: Preserve food in sealed cans or jars using an appropriate processing method.
words.example: The factory cans tomatoes during the harvest season.

words.definitionEn: Put food into containers or wrapping for storage, transport or sale.
words.example: The company packages its snacks in small bags.

words.definitionEn: Information attached to a product; also, to attach identifying information.
words.example: Read the label to see which ingredients the soup contains.

words.definitionEn: Changing raw food through physical, biological or chemical methods to make food products.
words.example: Drying fruit is one form of food processing.

words.definitionEn: Make something whiter or lighter, often using a chemical treatment.
words.example: Some producers bleach flour during processing.

words.definitionEn: Help a mixture maintain its texture or prevent its components from separating.
words.example: The manufacturer uses an ingredient that helps stabilize the sauce.

words.definitionEn: Remove most of the water from something.
words.example: The company dehydrates fruit to make lightweight snacks.

words.definitionEn: An uncommon wording meaning hide an odour; conceal or mask an odour is more natural.
words.example: The added flavouring can mask an unpleasant odour.

words.definitionEn: Make food or drink sweeter.
words.example: She uses a little honey to sweeten her tea.

words.term: Sap the original flavour out of a product
words.definitionEn: Gradually remove or weaken a product's original flavour; an expressive, critical phrase.
words.example: The reviewer complained that excessive processing had sapped the original flavour out of the product.

words.definitionEn: A cereal grain used in food, animal feed and drink production.
words.example: We added barley to the vegetable soup.

words.definitionEn: Spices crushed or powdered manually, for example with a mortar and pestle.
words.example: The cook used hand-ground spices in the curry.

words.definitionEn: Plant leaves used for flavour after their moisture has been removed.
words.example: Keep dried herbs in tightly closed containers.

words.definitionEn: Related to cooking or preparing food.
words.example: She wants to improve her culinary skills.

words.definitionEn: An unusual phrase for juice obtained by squeezing oranges; freshly squeezed orange juice is more idiomatic when made recently.
words.example: We served freshly squeezed orange juice with breakfast.

words.definitionEn: A smell resembling smoke from burning wood in a barbecue sauce; it does not prove actual wood-smoking.
words.translationUz: barbekyu sousining yog‘och tutuniga o‘xshash hidi
words.example: I noticed the wood-smoked aroma of the barbecue sauce immediately.

words.definitionEn: A taste or overall eating quality resembling cream; creamy often describes a smooth, rich texture.
words.example: The soup has a creamy taste even without added cream.

words.definitionEn: A flavour resembling butter.
words.example: The biscuits have a rich, buttery taste.

words.definitionEn: Foods made from animal milk, such as cheese, butter and yogurt.
words.example: The fridge has a separate shelf for dairy products.

words.definitionEn: Grassy fields receiving a lot of sunlight; a descriptive, evocative phrase.
words.example: The advertisement showed cows in sun-drenched meadows.

words.definitionEn: Outdoor cooking equipment used behind a home; especially American usage.
words.example: The smell of food rose from backyard grills across the neighbourhood.

words.definitionEn: Chemical substances that can have strong effects in small amounts; potent does not itself mean harmful.
words.translationUz: oz miqdorda ham kuchli ta’sir qiluvchi kimyoviy moddalar
words.example: The article describes flavour compounds as potent chemicals because tiny amounts can affect aroma.

words.definitionEn: The ability to detect smells; the sense of smell is the usual everyday expression.
words.example: Our olfactory senses help us recognise familiar food aromas.

words.definitionEn: A strong figurative expression for something presented as seriously damaging to health.
words.example: The columnist described the diet as an “assault on health.”

words.definitionEn: Something that may harm a person's health.
words.example: Poor food storage can be a health risk.

words.definitionEn: The person or thing responsible for a problem; often informal or figurative.
words.example: A faulty fridge was the culprit behind the spoiled food.

words.term: Keep us going throughout the day
words.definitionEn: Give us enough energy to continue our usual activities.
words.example: A filling breakfast helps keep us going throughout the day.

words.definitionEn: Long, thin pieces of dough cooked in liquid and eaten in many dishes.
words.example: We had noodles with vegetables for lunch.

words.definitionEn: Smooth-skinned fruits similar to peaches.
words.example: The fruit salad contains nectarines and grapes.

words.definitionEn: Thin, round flatbreads, usually made from maize or wheat flour.
words.example: We filled the tortillas with beans and salad.

words.definitionEn: A food made by coagulating soy milk and pressing the curds.
words.example: She added tofu to the vegetable stir-fry.

words.definitionEn: The category of fruit in a food-group system.
words.example: Apples and nectarines belong to the fruit group.

words.definitionEn: Preserved and sold in a sealed can, usually after heat processing.
words.example: Canned tomatoes are useful for making sauces.

words.definitionEn: Kept at a low enough temperature to freeze, usually for preservation.
words.example: We always keep frozen vegetables at home.

words.definitionEn: Dried grapes.
words.example: He sprinkled raisins over his oatmeal.

words.definitionEn: Dried plums.
words.example: She added chopped prunes to the cake mixture.

words.definitionEn: Plums that have lost moisture; dried plums is the normal food term, while dried-up can sound unappealing.
words.example: Prunes are dried plums; “dried-up plums” is a less natural food description.

words.definitionEn: Seeds of cereal crops, or the crops that produce them.
words.example: Whole grains are used in this bread.

words.definitionEn: A cereal grain often used to make porridge and breakfast foods.
words.example: She soaked the oats overnight.

words.definitionEn: A cereal crop whose grain is widely used to make flour.
words.example: Most of the bread in this shop is made from wheat.

words.definitionEn: A food made from oats; in American English, often cooked oat porridge.
words.example: I had oatmeal with banana for breakfast.

words.definitionEn: One whole lettuce plant sold as a tightly grouped set of leaves.
words.example: Please buy a head of lettuce for the salad.

words.definitionEn: Leaves that are firm and make a slight cracking sound when eaten.
words.example: The sandwich was filled with crunchy leaves and sliced cucumber.

words.definitionEn: A vegetable with long, tender green, white or purple shoots.
words.example: We served grilled asparagus with dinner.

words.definitionEn: Divide a category into smaller categories.
words.example: We can split this group into leafy and starchy vegetables.

words.definitionEn: A vegetable with dark green edible leaves.
words.example: She stirred fresh spinach into the soup.

words.definitionEn: Containing a lot of starch, a type of carbohydrate.
words.example: Potatoes are often described as a starchy food.

words.definitionEn: Edible roots that are commonly dark red; beets is American usage.
words.example: Roasted beets added colour to the salad.

words.definitionEn: Used after examples to show that there are many more.
words.example: We grow carrots, spinach and beans, just to name a few.

words.definitionEn: A nutrient needed to build and maintain body tissues, found in foods such as beans, eggs and meat.
words.example: Lentils provide protein in this meal.

words.definitionEn: A large sea fish commonly sold fresh or canned.
words.example: I made a tuna sandwich for lunch.

words.definitionEn: The category containing milk and related foods in some food-group systems.
words.example: Yogurt and cheese are usually placed in the dairy group.

words.definitionEn: A food made by fermenting milk with bacteria.
words.example: She served plain yogurt with fruit.

words.definitionEn: A flat piece cut from a pineapple.
words.example: He added a slice of pineapple to his plate.

words.definitionEn: Small pieces of pasta, often shaped like short tubes.
words.example: The children had macaroni with tomato sauce.

words.definitionEn: A small amount of food eaten between meals; also, to eat between meals.
words.example: I took an apple as a snack.

words.definitionEn: A trained professional who assesses diets and advises on nutrition; dietitian is the usual professional spelling.
words.example: The hospital dietitian discussed meal options with the patient.

words.definitionEn: Spend no more than the amount of money available or planned.
words.example: Planning meals can help you stay within your budget.

words.definitionEn: An overall eating pattern providing a suitable variety and balance of foods and nutrients.
words.example: A well-balanced diet can include many different cuisines.

words.definitionEn: Tablets containing one or more vitamins.
words.example: She asked a professional whether she needed vitamin pills.

words.definitionEn: Organic substances needed in small amounts for normal growth and health.
words.example: Different foods provide different vitamins.

words.definitionEn: The amount of something eaten or drunk over a period.
words.example: The diary helped him track his daily water intake.

words.definitionEn: Develop new, regular ways of choosing and eating food.
words.example: Preparing lunch at home helped her establish new eating habits.

words.definitionEn: Portions or measured amounts of food given to one person.
words.example: The recipe makes four servings.

words.definitionEn: Eat reasonable amounts without having too much.
words.example: He enjoys cake but tries to eat it in moderation.

words.definitionEn: Meat with relatively little fat.
words.example: The recipe suggests using lean meat.

words.definitionEn: Requirements or benchmarks intended to ensure food is safe to eat.
words.example: The factory trains workers to follow food safety standards.

words.definitionEn: Establish the level or rules that people or products should meet.
words.example: Authorities set standards for food handling.

words.definitionEn: Businesses involved in producing, processing, distributing and selling food.
words.example: Many local people work in the food industry.

words.definitionEn: Identify possible hazards and evaluate how likely and serious the harm could be.
words.example: The manager must carry out a risk assessment before changing the storage system.

words.definitionEn: Be vulnerable to contamination or effects caused by harmful bacteria; the precise meaning depends on the subject.
words.translationUz: zararli bakteriyalarga ta’sirchan yoki moyil bo‘lmoq
words.example: Food kept in unsuitable conditions may be susceptible to contamination by harmful bacteria.

words.definitionEn: Keep goods in a place until they are used or sold.
words.example: The shop stores products according to the instructions on their labels.

words.definitionEn: A large building where goods are stored before sale or distribution.
words.example: The deliveries are checked at the warehouse.

words.definitionEn: A refrigerated room or building used to keep perishable goods cold.
words.example: The dairy products are waiting in the cold store.

words.definitionEn: Foods preserved or sold in a frozen state.
words.example: The supermarket has an aisle for frozen foods.

words.definitionEn: Allow or cause frozen food to thaw; also, remove ice from a freezer.
words.example: Check the instructions before you defrost the fish.

words.term: Keep foods past their expiry date
words.definitionEn: Retain food after its stated expiry date; use-by and best-before labels have different meanings.
words.translationUz: yaroqlilik muddati o‘tgan oziq-ovqatni saqlab qo‘ymoq
words.example: The survey asked whether households keep foods past their expiry date.

words.definitionEn: Prepare, touch, move and store food in a household setting.
words.translationUz: uyda oziq-ovqat bilan xavfsiz muomala qilmoq
words.example: Students learn how to handle food at home safely.

words.definitionEn: The time a product can be stored under stated conditions while remaining suitable for use.
words.example: Packaging can affect a product's shelf life.

words.definitionEn: Below an acceptable or required level of quality.
words.example: Inspectors found substandard storage facilities.

words.definitionEn: Extremely large or impressive growth.
words.example: The town has seen a phenomenal expansion in food delivery services.

words.definitionEn: Food produced under organic standards, which restrict many synthetic inputs and specify production practices.
words.example: The shop sells both organic food and conventionally produced food.

words.definitionEn: Designed for wealthier customers or associated with higher prices; especially American usage.
words.example: They booked a table at an upscale restaurant.

words.definitionEn: Receive the most prominent attention or position; figurative.
words.example: Local vegetables get top billing on the restaurant's menu.

words.definitionEn: The study or process of obtaining and using food for growth and health.
words.example: The course introduces the basics of nutrition.

words.definitionEn: Teaching people how to prevent food-related illness through safe practices.
words.example: Food safety education is part of the staff training programme.

words.definitionEn: Containing spices that create a burning sensation in the mouth; hot can also mean high in temperature.
words.example: The curry was too spicy for me, so I ordered something milder.

words.definitionEn: Not strongly spicy or intense in flavour.
words.example: The children prefer a mild curry.

words.definitionEn: Tasting strongly of salt.
words.example: The soup was so salty that I could not finish it.

words.definitionEn: Containing or tasting of a lot of sugar.
words.example: I find this breakfast cereal too sugary.

words.definitionEn: Unpleasantly sweet or rich.
words.translationUz: haddan tashqari shirin va ko‘ngilni aynitadigan
words.example: The icing had a sickly taste.

words.definitionEn: Salty or spicy rather than sweet; savory is American spelling.
words.example: I prefer savoury snacks, such as crackers and cheese.

words.definitionEn: Having a sharp, acidic taste like lemon.
words.example: The sauce was sour, so she adjusted the recipe.

words.definitionEn: Having a strong, sharp taste like unsweetened coffee or some dark chocolate.
words.example: The coffee tasted bitter without milk.

words.definitionEn: Having a pleasant flavour.
words.example: The vegetable curry was surprisingly tasty.

words.definitionEn: Having little or no flavour.
words.example: The rice was tasteless until we added some sauce.

words.definitionEn: So pleasant to eat that you want more; informal British English.
words.example: These roasted nuts are very moreish.

words.definitionEn: Cooked for too long.
words.example: The pasta was overcooked and too soft.

words.definitionEn: Not cooked enough.
words.example: She returned the undercooked chicken to the kitchen.

words.definitionEn: Fully developed and ready to eat, especially fruit.
words.example: The peaches are ripe and ready to eat.

words.definitionEn: Not yet fully developed or ready to eat.
words.example: The unripe mango was hard and sharp-tasting.

words.definitionEn: Naturally ready to harvest and commonly available at a particular time of year.
words.example: Strawberries are cheaper when they are in season.

words.definitionEn: Become spoiled and no longer suitable to eat; informal British English.
words.example: The milk has gone off.

words.term: Heavy food or a heavy meal
words.definitionEn: Food that feels very filling and may be difficult to digest.
words.example: I do not want a heavy meal before travelling.

words.term: Light food or a light meal
words.definitionEn: A small or easily digested meal that does not feel too filling.
words.example: We had a light meal of soup and bread.

words.definitionEn: Heavy and filling, often because it contains a lot of starch; usually negative, especially British.
words.example: The pudding was a bit stodgy for my taste.

words.definitionEn: An eating pattern with an appropriate variety and balance of foods and nutrients; also well-balanced diet.
words.example: She is trying to maintain a balanced diet while studying.

words.definitionEn: An informal term for foods typically high in sugar, salt or fat and offering limited nutritional value.
words.example: He wants to replace some of his junk food snacks with fruit.

words.definitionEn: Suggesting that food is good for you; often a broad description rather than a precise claim.
words.example: The café advertises wholesome homemade lunches.

words.definitionEn: A marketing phrase suggesting that food has recently come from a farm; its meaning may be vague.
words.example: The box says “farm fresh,” but I still check the storage instructions.

words.definitionEn: Made at home; in marketing, sometimes used to suggest a home-style recipe.
words.example: She brought homemade bread to the picnic.

words.definitionEn: Foods that retain most of their natural components and are usually minimally processed.
words.example: The shop sells wholefoods such as oats, nuts and dried beans.

words.definitionEn: Foods that have undergone little or no processing; the exact meaning depends on context.
words.example: The lesson compares unprocessed foods with ready-made meals.

words.definitionEn: A broad description suggesting limited artificial intervention; natural alone does not establish safety or nutritional quality.
words.example: The shop promotes natural foods, but customers still need clear ingredient information.

words.definitionEn: Eggs or other animal products from animals allowed outdoor access under the relevant production system.
words.translationUz: erkin yaylovda boqilgan hayvon mahsulotlari; erkin yuruvchi tovuq tuxumi
words.example: The recipe uses free-range eggs.

words.definitionEn: Containing no gluten within the relevant standard; gluten is a protein found in wheat, barley and rye.
words.example: My guest needs gluten-free bread.

words.definitionEn: Manufactured colouring substances added to change a food's appearance.
words.example: The label says the drink contains no artificial colours.

words.term: Contains no artificial colours or preservatives
words.definitionEn: A product claim saying that neither artificial colouring nor preservatives have been added or are present as specified.
words.example: The soup label reads “contains no artificial colours or preservatives.”

words.definitionEn: An immune-system reaction to a particular food; different from food intolerance.
words.example: He told the waiter about his food allergy.

words.definitionEn: Having an allergy caused by a particular substance.
words.example: She is allergic to peanuts.

words.definitionEn: A person who does not eat meat or fish; also describes food suitable for such a person.
words.translationUz: go‘sht va baliq yemaydigan kishi; vegetarian
words.example: The restaurant offers a vegetarian main course.

words.definitionEn: A person who avoids animal-derived foods and typically other animal products; also describes suitable food.
words.translationUz: hayvon mahsulotlarini iste’mol qilmaydigan kishi; vegan
words.example: We made a vegan curry with chickpeas and coconut milk.

words.definitionEn: Someone who does not eat meat; ask about fish and other requirements rather than assuming.
words.example: As a non-meat-eater, she always checks the menu before booking.

words.definitionEn: The well-being and humane treatment of animals.
words.example: Animal welfare influences his choice of eggs.

words.definitionEn: An intensive system associated especially with keeping laying hens in rows of cages.
words.example: The article discusses animal welfare concerns linked to battery farming.

words.definitionEn: Foods designed to require little time or effort to prepare.
words.example: Convenience foods are useful when people have limited time to cook.

words.definitionEn: Meals prepared in advance and sold ready to eat or heat.
words.example: She keeps a few ready-made meals for busy evenings.

words.definitionEn: A condition involving excessive body fat that can impair health.
words.example: The lecture discussed obesity as a complex public health issue.

words.definitionEn: Labels giving information about a food's energy and nutrient content.
words.example: Nutrition labels help shoppers compare similar products.

words.definitionEn: A system using red, amber and green to indicate high, medium and low levels of selected nutrients.
words.translationUz: svetofor ranglari bilan oziqlanish qiymatini belgilash
words.example: Traffic-light labelling makes it easier to compare salt levels.

words.definitionEn: Trading arrangements intended to support fairer terms and conditions for producers; certification schemes set specific requirements.
words.example: She looks for fair trade coffee when shopping.

words.term: Book a table or make a reservation
words.definitionEn: Arrange in advance to have a table kept for you at a restaurant.
words.example: We should book a table for Saturday evening.

words.definitionEn: Tell a restaurant that you no longer need the arrangement you made.
words.example: I called to cancel our reservation because two guests were ill.

words.definitionEn: One stage of a meal, served separately from the others.
words.example: The restaurant offers a three-course lunch.

words.definitionEn: A small dish served before the main part of a meal.
words.example: I ordered soup as a starter.

words.definitionEn: The principal dish in a meal.
words.example: For my main course, I chose grilled fish.

words.definitionEn: Sweet food served at the end of a meal.
words.example: We shared a chocolate dessert.

words.definitionEn: A smaller dish served alongside the main dish.
words.example: Would you like a vegetable side dish with your chicken?

words.definitionEn: A fixed selection of dishes offered for a set price.
words.example: The set menu includes a starter and a main course.

words.definitionEn: Choose separately priced dishes from the menu rather than a fixed meal.
words.translationUz: menyudan taomlarni alohida tanlab buyurtma qilmoq
words.example: We decided to order à la carte.

words.definitionEn: Dishes offered in addition to the regular menu, often for a limited time.
words.example: Ask the waiter what today's specials are.

words.definitionEn: Provide food suitable for people with those dietary preferences or requirements.
words.translationUz: vegetarian yoki veganlarga mos ovqat taklif qilmoq
words.example: The café caters for vegans as well as vegetarians.

words.definitionEn: A person who invites and looks after guests.
words.example: Our host offered us another serving of soup.

words.definitionEn: An additional helping of food after the first; informal.
words.example: The stew was so good that everyone wanted seconds.

words.definitionEn: Take the food or drink you want without waiting to be served.
words.example: Please help yourself to some salad.

words.definitionEn: Avoid eating so much that you cannot enjoy dessert; often keep a bit of room for pudding.
words.example: Keep room for dessert because we have made an apple pie.

words.term: Pudding or a sweet or afters
words.definitionEn: British terms for dessert; afters is informal, and pudding can also name particular dishes.
words.example: What are we having for pudding?

words.definitionEn: Fill a person's glass again or add more drink.
words.example: Can I refill your glass with water?

words.definitionEn: Tell me when to stop pouring or serving; informal.
words.example: I will pour the juice; say when.

words.definitionEn: An informal response to say when, meaning that enough has been served.
words.example: “Say when.” “When! That is enough, thank you.”

words.definitionEn: Utensils used for eating, especially knives, forks and spoons.
words.example: Could we have some clean cutlery, please?

words.definitionEn: A small cloth or paper used to protect clothing and wipe the mouth during a meal.
words.example: He placed his napkin on his lap.

words.definitionEn: Divide the cost of a meal between the people eating.
words.example: Shall we split the bill equally?

words.term: Lunch or dinner is on me
words.definitionEn: I will pay for the meal; informal.
words.translationUz: tushlik yoki kechki ovqat hisobini men to‘layman
words.example: You paid last time, so dinner is on me tonight.

words.definitionEn: Let me pay for this; informal.
words.example: Put your wallet away; let me get this.

words.definitionEn: Eat dinner together with us.
words.example: Would you like to join us for dinner tomorrow?

words.definitionEn: Accept our invitation, often with the implication that we will pay; polite.
words.example: Please be our guest for lunch after the meeting.

words.definitionEn: Be entertained with generous meals and drinks, often by a host or organization.
words.translationUz: hashamatli taom va ichimliklar bilan mehmon qilinmoq
words.example: The visiting team was wined and dined by the organizers.

words.definitionEn: Service so good that it is difficult to find fault with it.
words.example: The restaurant is known for its impeccable service.

words.definitionEn: Service that is unusually slow.
words.example: The food was excellent, but the service was sluggish.

words.definitionEn: Polite and respectful.
words.example: The waiter was courteous even when the restaurant became busy.

words.definitionEn: Too controlling, forceful or insistent in dealing with others.
words.translationUz: haddan tashqari hukmronlik qiluvchi; bosim o‘tkazuvchi
words.example: The waiter was helpful without being overbearing.

words.definitionEn: Looking unhappy or bad-tempered and unwilling to speak.
words.example: The server seemed sullen throughout the meal.

words.definitionEn: Abrupt in speech or manner, sometimes seeming rude.
words.example: The manager gave us a brusque reply.

words.definitionEn: Making someone feel less interested or comfortable; informal.
words.example: The dirty tables were rather off-putting.

words.definitionEn: Make a special effort to help or please someone.
words.example: The staff went out of their way to accommodate our group.

words.definitionEn: Like sweet foods very much.
words.example: I have a sweet tooth, so choosing dessert is easy.

words.definitionEn: Pay close attention to the energy content of what you eat.
words.example: She reads labels carefully when she is counting the calories.

words.definitionEn: Aware of and attentive to the calories in food.
words.example: The menu includes smaller portions for calorie-conscious diners.

words.definitionEn: An amount of food served to one person.
words.example: Could I have a smaller portion of rice?

words.definitionEn: Someone who is very particular about food and rejects many foods; informal.
words.example: My brother is a fussy eater who dislikes most sauces.

words.definitionEn: Never drinking alcohol.
words.example: He is teetotal, so we ordered sparkling water.

words.definitionEn: Specific needs or restrictions affecting what someone can eat.
words.example: Please tell us about any dietary requirements before the event.

words.definitionEn: Have or do more than is sensible; informal.
words.example: The cake is delicious, but I do not want to overdo it.

words.definitionEn: Accept whatever food is available without choosing or expecting special preparation; informal British usage.
words.translationUz: bor ovqatga qanoat qilmoq; nima chiqsa shuni yemoq
words.example: Come over for dinner, but you will have to take pot luck.

words.definitionEn: Bring a bottle of drink to a gathering, usually wine unless another drink is specified.
words.translationUz: ziyofatga bir shisha ichimlik olib kelmoq
words.example: They asked us to bring a bottle to the dinner party.

words.definitionEn: A social event at someone's home where guests are served dinner.
words.example: They invited six friends to a dinner party.

words.definitionEn: A relaxed social meeting or gathering.
words.example: We are having an informal get-together with a few snacks.

words.definitionEn: Small snacks, often served before a meal or with drinks; informal.
words.example: There are some nibbles on the table.

words.definitionEn: Have something to eat quickly; informal.
words.example: We can grab a bite to eat before class.

words.definitionEn: Buy a prepared meal to eat elsewhere; British English, takeout in American English.
words.example: We were too tired to cook, so we got a takeaway.

words.definitionEn: A combination of conditions likely to lead to a very bad result.
words.translationUz: falokatga olib kelishi aniq bo‘lgan holat
words.example: Inviting twenty people without planning the food is a recipe for disaster.

words.definitionEn: A combination of conditions likely to produce a good result.
words.example: Clear goals and regular practice are a recipe for success.

words.definitionEn: Invent an explanation, often a dishonest one; informal.
words.example: He cooked up a story about why he had missed the lesson.

words.definitionEn: Contain the features needed for a particular result; figurative.
words.translationUz: biror natija uchun zarur barcha jihatlarga ega bo‘lmoq
words.example: The café has all the ingredients of a successful business.

words.term: Let someone stew or stew in your own juice
words.definitionEn: Leave someone to worry about a problem, especially one they caused; informal.
words.translationUz: kimnidir o‘z muammosi bilan yolg‘iz qoldirmoq
words.example: After his rude remark, she let him stew for a while.

words.definitionEn: Not something I enjoy or find interesting; informal.
words.example: Very formal dinner parties are not my cup of tea.

words.definitionEn: Question someone intensely; informal figurative meaning, alongside the literal cooking meaning.
words.example: My friends grilled me about the restaurant I had visited.

words.definitionEn: An idea that has not been thought through properly; informal and critical.
words.example: Opening a café without a budget sounded like a half-baked idea.

words.definitionEn: Make something more lively or interesting; informal figurative meaning.
words.example: We added a cooking challenge to spice up the lesson.

words.definitionEn: People whose behaviour seems dishonest or morally unpleasant; negative.
words.example: The story involves a restaurant owner and several unsavoury characters.

words.definitionEn: Become unpleasant or unsuccessful after starting well.
words.example: Their business relationship turned sour over money.

words.definitionEn: Interesting or exciting stories about other people's private lives; informal.
words.example: They exchanged juicy gossip over lunch.

words.definitionEn: Categories of foods with shared nutritional or other characteristics.
words.example: The students sorted the ingredients into food groups.

words.definitionEn: Aroma is smell; flavour is the combined experience of taste, smell and other sensations when eating.
words.example: The bread's aroma was inviting, but its flavour was disappointing.

words.definitionEn: Microscopic organisms that can cause harm, including some that cause foodborne illness.
words.example: Safe food handling helps prevent the spread of harmful bacteria.

words.definitionEn: A date indicating when food should be used for safety under the stated storage conditions.
words.example: Check the use-by date and storage instructions on the chicken.

words.definitionEn: A date indicating how long a product is expected to retain its stated quality under proper storage.
words.translationUz: eng yaxshi sifat saqlanadigan muddat sanasi
words.example: The biscuit packet has a best-before date.

words.definitionEn: The presence or introduction of unwanted harmful substances or organisms.
words.example: The training explains how to prevent contamination in the kitchen.

words.definitionEn: Changes that make food unsuitable or unpleasant to eat.
words.example: Proper storage helps reduce food spoilage.

words.definitionEn: Food prepared in advance and sold ready to eat or heat.
words.example: Ready-made food saves her time on busy evenings.

words.definitionEn: Food additives that help maintain texture, consistency or a stable mixture.
words.example: The ice cream label lists several stabilizers.

words.definitionEn: Be associated with greenhouse gas emissions from production, use or other stages.
words.translationUz: uglerod izi; issiqxona gazlari chiqindisi bilan bog‘liq bo‘lmoq
words.example: Both growing and transporting food have a carbon footprint.

words.definitionEn: A physical or mental change that may indicate an illness.
words.example: A persistent cough can be a symptom of several illnesses.

words.definitionEn: An area of irritated skin, often with red spots.
words.example: A rash appeared on her arm.

words.definitionEn: A dark mark caused by bleeding beneath the skin after an injury.
words.example: He had a bruise on his leg after the fall.

words.definitionEn: A swelling or raised area in or under the skin.
words.example: She asked the doctor to examine a lump on her arm.

words.definitionEn: Small raised marks on the skin.
words.example: He noticed some spots on his face.

words.definitionEn: Dark bruising around an eye after an injury.
words.example: The ball hit her face and gave her a black eye.

words.definitionEn: Pain or irritation in the passage at the back of the mouth.
words.example: I have a sore throat and find swallowing uncomfortable.

words.definitionEn: Pain in the head.
words.example: She went home because she had a headache.

words.definitionEn: Pain in the back.
words.example: He developed backache after lifting heavy boxes.

words.definitionEn: Pain inside an ear.
words.example: The child could not sleep because of earache.

words.definitionEn: A common viral illness affecting the nose and throat.
words.example: I caught a cold during the holidays.

words.definitionEn: A viral illness that can cause fever, body aches and tiredness.
words.example: Several students were absent with flu.

words.definitionEn: An illness caused when harmful microorganisms enter and multiply in the body.
words.example: The doctor examined her ear infection.

words.definitionEn: A tiny infectious agent that reproduces inside living cells.
words.example: A virus caused the outbreak.

words.definitionEn: Skin damage caused by too much exposure to the sun.
words.example: His shoulders were red with sunburn.

words.definitionEn: To feel that you might vomit.
words.example: I felt sick during the journey.

words.definitionEn: To feel unsteady or as if your surroundings are spinning.
words.example: She felt dizzy when she stood up.

words.definitionEn: To have difficulty getting enough air.
words.example: He felt breathless after climbing the stairs.

words.definitionEn: To feel extremely tired.
words.example: She felt exhausted after the night shift.

words.definitionEn: To feel very low or unhappy; in a medical context, this may refer to depression.
words.example: He told his doctor that he had been feeling depressed.

words.definitionEn: To feel under mental or emotional pressure.
words.example: She felt stressed before her exams.

words.definitionEn: To stop wanting to eat.
words.example: He lost his appetite while he was ill.

words.definitionEn: To become temporarily unable to speak normally.
words.example: She lost her voice after the concert.

words.definitionEn: To have an irritating skin sensation / to rub the skin to relieve it.
words.example: My arm itches, but I am trying not to scratch it.

words.definitionEn: To shake slightly, often because of cold or fever.
words.example: He began to shiver despite the warm room.

words.definitionEn: To shake involuntarily, for example through fear, weakness or illness.
words.example: Her hands were trembling as she held the cup.

words.definitionEn: To cause or experience physical pain.
words.example: My knee hurts when I bend it.

words.definitionEn: To have a continuous, usually dull pain.
words.example: My legs ached after the long walk.

words.definitionEn: To bring the contents of the stomach out through the mouth.
words.example: He vomited twice during the night.

words.definitionEn: To suddenly force air out through the nose and mouth.
words.example: Dust makes her sneeze.

words.definitionEn: A person receiving medical care.
words.example: The nurse asked the patient to sit down.

words.definitionEn: A person qualified to diagnose and treat illnesses.
words.example: The physician reviewed his medical history.

words.definitionEn: A trained professional who provides care for patients.
words.example: A nurse checked her temperature.

words.definitionEn: A professional who treats teeth and gums.
words.example: The dentist repaired the damaged tooth.

words.definitionEn: A professional who supplies and fits glasses; some also test sight.
words.example: The optician adjusted the frames of my glasses.

words.definitionEn: A doctor trained to perform operations.
words.example: The surgeon explained the procedure.

words.definitionEn: A place where people receive medical treatment, including inpatient care.
words.example: She stayed in hospital for two nights.

words.definitionEn: A place providing medical consultations or treatment, often for a particular service.
words.example: He attends a diabetes clinic.

words.definitionEn: A shop or service that supplies medicines.
words.example: She collected her medicine from the pharmacy.

words.definitionEn: A medicine used to reduce pain.
words.example: The pharmacist explained how to take the painkiller.

words.definitionEn: A small solid dose of medicine that is swallowed or otherwise taken as directed.
words.example: The medicine comes in tablet form.

words.definitionEn: Medicine or another substance given through a needle.
words.example: The nurse prepared the injection.

words.definitionEn: A strip of material used to cover or support an injured body part.
words.example: He wore a bandage around his wrist.

words.definitionEn: A written or electronic instruction authorising the supply of medicine.
words.example: The doctor wrote a prescription.

words.definitionEn: An instrument used to measure temperature.
words.example: She used a thermometer to check his temperature.

words.definitionEn: Discomfort in the upper abdomen associated with digestion.
words.example: He complained of indigestion after dinner.

words.definitionEn: Digestive discomfort, sometimes with nausea or diarrhoea.
words.example: She stayed home with an upset stomach.

words.definitionEn: An illness or symptom involving frequent loose, watery stools.
words.example: The infection caused diarrhoea.

words.definitionEn: Vomiting or nausea together with frequent watery stools.
words.translationUz: ko'ngil aynishi yoki qusish bilan birga ich ketishi
words.example: Several guests reported sickness and diarrhoea.

words.definitionEn: Painful sensations in the area between the neck and abdomen.
words.example: The patient described repeated chest pains.

words.definitionEn: Pressure of the blood against artery walls above / below the expected range.
words.example: The nurse recorded his blood pressure.

words.definitionEn: A body temperature higher than normal, often during illness.
words.example: The child developed a fever overnight.

words.definitionEn: An allergic reaction to pollen that commonly affects the nose and eyes.
words.example: Her hay fever gets worse in spring.

words.definitionEn: An immune reaction to a substance that is usually harmless.
words.example: He has an allergy to dust mites.

words.definitionEn: To fracture a bone in the joint area connecting the hand and arm.
words.example: She broke her wrist while skating.

words.definitionEn: To injure the ligaments around the joint above the foot.
words.translationUz: to'pig'ining paylarini cho'zib yoki shikastlab olmoq
words.example: He sprained his ankle on uneven ground.

words.definitionEn: To force the upper-arm bone out of its normal position at the shoulder joint.
words.example: She dislocated her shoulder in the fall.

words.definitionEn: Difficulty or discomfort when moving the neck.
words.example: He woke up with a stiff neck.

words.definitionEn: To turn a joint awkwardly and possibly injure it.
words.example: She twisted her ankle on the steps.

words.definitionEn: A nose through which it is difficult to breathe because of congestion.
words.example: I could not sleep with my bunged-up nose.

words.definitionEn: To arrange a time to see a healthcare professional.
words.example: He called to make an appointment with his GP.

words.definitionEn: To explain the changes or discomfort you are experiencing.
words.example: The doctor asked her to describe her symptoms.

words.definitionEn: To have a blood sample taken and examined.
words.example: He had a blood test at the clinic.

words.definitionEn: To officially order medicine for a patient.
words.example: The doctor prescribed medication for the infection.

words.definitionEn: To use a medicine according to its instructions.
words.example: She takes her medicine at the same time each day.

words.definitionEn: An amount filling a teaspoon; in medicine, a measured dose typically equal to 5 ml.
words.example: The label specified one measured teaspoonful.

words.term: At bedtime / last thing at night
words.definitionEn: Immediately before going to sleep.
words.example: The instructions said to take the tablet at bedtime.

words.definitionEn: To wrap or cover an injured area with protective material.
words.example: The nurse put a bandage on his hand.

words.definitionEn: To undergo a surgical procedure.
words.example: She had an operation on her knee.

words.definitionEn: To perform surgery on someone.
words.example: The surgeon operated on the patient that morning.

words.term: To have your leg put in plaster
words.definitionEn: To have a hard cast applied to support an injured leg.
words.example: He had his leg put in plaster after the accident.

words.definitionEn: To heal or become sound again after damage.
words.example: The broken bone took several weeks to mend.

words.definitionEn: To become well again after being ill.
words.example: He is recovering from a chest infection.

words.definitionEn: To return to health after an illness.
words.example: It took her a week to get over the virus.

words.definitionEn: To spend a day away from work or study.
words.translationUz: bir kun dam olish; ish yoki o'qishdan ruxsat olmoq
words.example: He took a day off because he felt unwell.

words.definitionEn: A pattern of eating that supports health and provides appropriate nutrients.
words.example: The lesson focused on maintaining a healthy diet.

words.definitionEn: Fish containing relatively high amounts of oil in their tissues.
words.example: Salmon is an example of oily fish.

words.definitionEn: Bread made from flour containing all parts of the grain.
words.example: She chose wholemeal bread for her sandwich.

words.definitionEn: Foods containing a large amount of sugar.
words.example: The survey asked how often children ate sugary foods.

words.definitionEn: Drinks containing bubbles of gas.
words.example: The café sells water, juice and fizzy drinks.

words.definitionEn: Food changed from its original state through manufacturing or preparation.
words.example: The class compared labels on processed foods.

words.definitionEn: Manufactured substances added to change the colour of food.
words.example: The packaging listed several artificial colours.

words.definitionEn: To treat or store food so that it lasts longer without spoiling.
words.example: Freezing is one way to preserve food.

words.definitionEn: Foods containing a high proportion of fat.
words.example: The questionnaire included a question about fatty foods.

words.definitionEn: Fruits such as oranges and lemons.
words.example: The market sells a wide range of citrus fruits.

words.definitionEn: Organic nutrients needed in small amounts for normal body functions.
words.example: The chart showed which foods contained different vitamins.

words.term: A high fat / salt / sugar content
words.definitionEn: A large proportion of fat, salt or sugar in a food.
words.example: The label showed that the snack had a high salt content.

words.definitionEn: In large amounts.
words.example: The factory produces food in large quantities.

words.definitionEn: To eat, drink or use something.
words.example: The survey measured how much sugar people consumed.

words.definitionEn: A popular marketing term for foods presented as especially beneficial to health.
words.translationUz: juda foydali deb targ'ib qilinadigan oziq-ovqatlar
words.example: The article questioned claims made about superfoods.

words.definitionEn: To maintain good physical condition, usually through regular activity.
words.example: She cycles to work to keep fit.

words.definitionEn: The condition of being physically able to exercise and carry out activities.
words.example: He wants to improve his fitness.

words.term: To take exercise / get regular exercise
words.definitionEn: To do physical activity regularly.
words.example: She tries to get regular exercise each week.

words.definitionEn: To do physical activity on a consistent basis.
words.example: They exercise regularly at the local sports centre.

words.definitionEn: Physical activity that forms part of everyday life.
words.example: Walking to school provides routine daily exercise.

words.term: To maintain a good level of fitness
words.definitionEn: To keep your physical condition at a satisfactory standard.
words.example: He swims to maintain a good level of fitness.

words.definitionEn: The state of a person's emotional and psychological wellbeing.
words.example: The course discusses mental health at work.

words.definitionEn: The condition and functioning of the body.
words.example: The survey asked about participants' physical health.

words.definitionEn: Mental or emotional pressure / causing that pressure.
words.example: She found the move stressful and needed time to manage her stress.

words.definitionEn: A mental health condition involving persistent low mood or loss of interest, among other symptoms.
words.example: He received support for depression.

words.definitionEn: Having an excessive amount of body fat / the condition of having it.
words.example: The report examined factors associated with obesity.

words.definitionEn: Obesity affecting children.
words.example: The researchers studied childhood obesity.

words.definitionEn: Repeated behaviours that have undesirable effects.
words.example: The class discussed ways of changing bad habits.

words.definitionEn: Damage or injury / causing damage or injury.
words.example: The poster described the harmful effects of tobacco smoke.

words.definitionEn: For an extended length of time.
words.example: The study followed participants over a long period.

words.definitionEn: To stop diseases from developing or spreading.
words.example: The programme aims to prevent diseases through vaccination.

words.term: To improve mental and physical health
words.definitionEn: To make emotional wellbeing and bodily health better.
words.example: The project explores ways to improve mental and physical health.

words.definitionEn: The ability to retain information briefly.
words.example: The task measured short-term memory.

words.definitionEn: The changes that occur as a person grows older.
words.example: The lecture examined the ageing process.

words.definitionEn: To reduce the speed of changes associated with growing older.
words.example: The advertisement claimed the product could slow the ageing process.

words.term: A good source of vitamin C
words.definitionEn: A food providing a useful amount of this vitamin.
words.example: The textbook describes citrus fruit as a good source of vitamin C.

words.definitionEn: Containing a relatively large amount of vitamin A.
words.example: The chart identifies foods high in vitamin A.

words.definitionEn: A fatty substance found in the blood and body cells.
words.example: The test measured her cholesterol level.

words.definitionEn: To reduce the amount of cholesterol, usually referring to its level in the blood.
words.example: The doctor discussed a plan to lower his cholesterol.

words.definitionEn: The body's network of defences against infection and disease.
words.example: Researchers study how the immune system responds to infection.

words.definitionEn: To increase the activity or effectiveness of the body's defences; often used loosely in health claims.
words.example: The advertisement claimed that the supplement could boost the immune system.

words.term: To reduce the risk of heart disease
words.definitionEn: To lower the likelihood of developing disease affecting the heart.
words.example: The campaign discusses ways to reduce the risk of heart disease.

words.definitionEn: Important positive effects on health.
words.example: The study investigated the activity's potential major health benefits.

words.term: To form part of a healthy diet
words.definitionEn: To be included within an overall pattern of balanced eating.
words.example: The leaflet explains how nuts can form part of a healthy diet.

words.term: An increased risk of heart attacks
words.definitionEn: A greater likelihood of experiencing a sudden interruption of blood supply to the heart.
words.example: The study reported an increased risk of heart attacks in one group.

words.definitionEn: Services provided to maintain health and treat illness.
words.example: Access to healthcare varies between regions.

words.definitionEn: People whose work involves providing health services.
words.example: Healthcare professionals attended the training session.

words.definitionEn: First-contact healthcare, such as care provided by a family doctor.
words.example: The new centre provides primary care.

words.definitionEn: Specialist healthcare, often accessed after a referral.
words.example: The report compared primary and secondary care.

words.term: A GP / general practitioner / family doctor
words.definitionEn: A doctor who treats common health problems and refers patients when necessary.
words.example: Her GP referred her to a specialist.

words.definitionEn: A professional, especially a doctor, temporarily covering another person's job.
words.example: A locum saw patients while the doctor was away.

words.definitionEn: A medical professional with expertise in a particular field.
words.example: He saw a specialist about his skin condition.

words.definitionEn: The premises where a doctor sees patients, especially in British English.
words.example: The doctor's surgery opens at eight.

words.definitionEn: The treatment of disease or injury through operations.
words.example: The injury required surgery.

words.definitionEn: To visit patients where they live to provide care.
words.example: The practice does home visits when appropriate.

words.term: To refer someone to a specialist
words.definitionEn: To direct a patient to a professional with particular expertise.
words.example: The GP referred him to a specialist.

words.definitionEn: To focus professionally on a particular subject or field.
words.example: She specialises in children's health.

words.definitionEn: A service paid for with public money.
words.example: The report discusses a state-funded health service.

words.definitionEn: Medical care paid for privately / to choose that form of care.
words.translationUz: xususiy tibbiyot / xususiy tibbiyot xizmatidan foydalanmoq
words.example: He decided to go private for the consultation.

words.definitionEn: An arrangement providing financial cover for specified costs or risks.
words.example: Her employer offers a health insurance scheme.

words.definitionEn: Supports held under the arms or by the hands to help someone walk.
words.example: He used crutches while his ankle healed.

words.definitionEn: A chair with wheels for a person who has difficulty walking.
words.example: The entrance is accessible to wheelchair users.

words.definitionEn: Lenses worn in a frame to improve sight.
words.example: She wears spectacles for reading.

words.definitionEn: Small corrective lenses worn directly on the eyes.
words.example: He switched from glasses to contact lenses.

words.definitionEn: The ability to see.
words.example: The optician checked her eyesight.

words.definitionEn: To improve difficulties with seeing by using treatment or visual aids.
words.example: The lenses help correct vision problems.

words.definitionEn: A device worn to make sounds easier to hear.
words.example: Her hearing aid helps her follow conversations.

words.definitionEn: An implanted device that helps control the heartbeat.
words.example: The doctor checked his pacemaker.

words.definitionEn: A manufactured joint used to replace a damaged natural one.
words.example: She received an artificial hip.

words.definitionEn: An artificial replacement for a missing leg.
words.example: He is learning to walk with a prosthetic leg.

words.definitionEn: A mechanical arm or hand controlled by a system.
words.example: The team demonstrated a robotic hand.

words.definitionEn: Equipment that produces images of the inside of the body.
words.example: The hospital installed a new medical scanner.

words.definitionEn: Radiation used to create images of structures inside the body, or the resulting images.
words.example: The dentist examined the X-rays.

words.definitionEn: Energy transmitted as waves or particles.
words.example: The course covered the use of radiation in medicine.

words.definitionEn: Equipment designed for a medical purpose.
words.example: The company manufactures medical devices.

words.definitionEn: A medicine that produces unconsciousness for an operation.
words.example: The procedure was performed under a general anaesthetic.

words.definitionEn: Not awake and unable to respond normally to the surroundings.
words.example: He was unconscious when help arrived.

words.definitionEn: An operation using a concentrated beam of light.
words.example: The clinic offers certain types of laser surgery.

words.definitionEn: An operation performed through small openings using special instruments.
words.example: She underwent keyhole surgery.

words.definitionEn: A body structure with a particular function, such as the heart.
words.example: The heart is an organ that pumps blood.

words.definitionEn: A group of cells forming part of the body.
words.example: The laboratory examined a sample of tissue.

words.definitionEn: The place where two or more bones meet.
words.example: The injury affected the knee joint.

words.definitionEn: An abnormal mass of tissue that may be benign or malignant.
words.example: The doctors examined the tumour.

words.definitionEn: To take an abnormal mass of tissue out of the body.
words.example: The surgeon removed the tumour.

words.definitionEn: Damage to heart muscle caused by a blocked or severely reduced blood supply.
words.example: He was treated in hospital after a heart attack.

words.definitionEn: Brain injury caused by blocked blood flow or bleeding in the brain.
words.example: She received rehabilitation after a stroke.

words.definitionEn: A group of conditions affecting the heart.
words.example: The research focuses on heart disease.

words.definitionEn: An illness or health problem that develops suddenly or lasts a relatively short time.
words.example: The service treats acute conditions.

words.definitionEn: A health problem that continues for a long time.
words.translationUz: surunkali holat; uzoq davom etadigan kasallik
words.example: He receives ongoing care for a chronic condition.

words.definitionEn: Long-term inflammation of the bronchial tubes associated with a persistent productive cough.
words.example: The patient was being treated for chronic bronchitis.

words.definitionEn: A medical doctor specialising in eye conditions.
words.example: The ophthalmologist examined her eyes.

words.definitionEn: A doctor specialising in the heart.
words.example: A cardiologist reviewed the test results.

words.definitionEn: A medical doctor specialising in mental health conditions.
words.example: She had an appointment with a psychiatrist.

words.definitionEn: A doctor specialising in skin conditions.
words.example: The dermatologist examined the rash.

words.definitionEn: A doctor specialising in the female reproductive system.
words.example: Her GP referred her to a gynaecologist.

words.definitionEn: A doctor specialising in pregnancy and childbirth.
words.example: The obstetrician discussed the birth plan.

words.definitionEn: A doctor specialising in children's health.
words.example: The paediatrician examined the baby.

words.definitionEn: A medical professional specialising in administering anaesthesia and related care.
words.example: The anaesthetist spoke to him before the operation.

words.definitionEn: A practitioner who inserts fine needles at selected points of the body.
words.example: She made an appointment with an acupuncturist.

words.definitionEn: A practitioner who uses manual techniques, especially involving the spine and joints.
words.translationUz: manual muolaja, ayniqsa umurtqa bilan shug'ullanuvchi mutaxassis; kiropraktik
words.example: He consulted a chiropractor about his back.

words.definitionEn: A doctor who practises a system using highly diluted preparations.
words.example: The article interviewed a homeopathic doctor.

words.definitionEn: A practitioner who uses aromatic oils, often in massage.
words.example: The aromatherapist explained which oils she used.

words.definitionEn: Treatments used instead of conventional medical care.
words.example: The article compared different forms of alternative medicine.

words.definitionEn: Treatments used alongside conventional medical care.
words.example: The survey asked about the use of complementary medicine.

words.definitionEn: Mainstream medical practice based on established clinical approaches.
words.example: The chapter contrasted conventional Western medicine with other approaches.

words.definitionEn: To feel ill; the second expression is informal.
words.translationUz: o'zini yomon his qilmoq / betobroq bo'lmoq
words.example: She felt poorly and stayed at home.

words.definitionEn: To feel slightly ill or look less healthy than usual.
words.example: I have been feeling off-colour all morning.

words.definitionEn: To feel mildly unwell or not like your usual self.
words.translationUz: o'zini biroz betob yoki xomush his qilmoq
words.example: He felt out of sorts after a sleepless night.

words.definitionEn: To feel slightly ill.
words.example: She is feeling under the weather today.

words.definitionEn: To resist an illness or overcome it as it begins.
words.translationUz: kasallikka qarshi kurashmoq; uni yengib o'tmoq
words.example: I think I am fighting off a cold.

words.term: To go down with / come down with an illness
words.definitionEn: To begin to suffer from an illness.
words.translationUz: kasallikka chalinib qolmoq / kasallik yuqtirib olmoq
words.example: He came down with flu over the weekend.

words.definitionEn: To catch an infectious illness; informal.
words.example: She picked up a bug while travelling.

words.definitionEn: To become infected.
words.example: Several colleagues caught the same virus.

words.definitionEn: To experience an illness or ongoing health problem.
words.example: She suffers from hay fever.

words.definitionEn: To be recovering after illness or injury.
words.example: He is on the mend after his operation.

words.definitionEn: To have passed the most difficult stage of an illness or problem.
words.translationUz: kasallikning eng og'ir davridan o'tib olmoq
words.example: She is still tired but is over the worst.

words.term: To be back on your feet
words.definitionEn: To be well or active again after illness or difficulty.
words.example: He hopes to be back on his feet soon.

words.definitionEn: Various minor bodily pains.
words.example: She complained of aches and pains after the hike.

words.definitionEn: Minor injuries involving broken skin and dark marks.
words.example: He escaped with a few cuts and bruises.

words.definitionEn: I feel as though my head or surroundings are turning.
words.example: I need to sit down; my head is spinning.

words.definitionEn: A continuous pain that is not sharp.
words.example: There was a dull ache in his shoulder.

words.definitionEn: A persistent pain that continues to bother you.
words.example: She described a nagging ache in her back.

words.definitionEn: Pain that seems to beat or pulse.
words.example: He had a throbbing ache in his tooth.

words.definitionEn: A sharp, burning sensation.
words.example: She felt a stinging pain around the scratch.

words.definitionEn: To hurt with a repeated beating sensation.
words.example: My head was throbbing after the long day.

words.definitionEn: Having or feeling as though you have a raised body temperature.
words.example: He felt hot and feverish.

words.definitionEn: Feeling shaky with cold or fever.
words.example: She felt shivery and wrapped herself in a blanket.

words.definitionEn: Feeling as though you might vomit.
words.example: The journey made him feel nauseous.

words.definitionEn: Nights spent unable to sleep.
words.example: The discomfort caused several sleepless nights.

words.definitionEn: An illness or symptom disappears or improves completely.
words.translationUz: kasallik yoki alomat yo'qolib, tuzalib ketmoq
words.example: The rash cleared up after treatment.

words.definitionEn: A sudden episode of inflammation of the appendix.
words.example: He was admitted with an acute attack of appendicitis.

words.definitionEn: To undergo an operation to take out the appendix.
words.example: She had her appendix removed last year.

words.definitionEn: To become infected with a disease; a formal expression.
