words.example: Several travellers contracted an illness abroad.

words.definitionEn: To have a disease as the cause of death.
words.example: The historical account described people who died of the disease.

words.definitionEn: Strong emotional pain rather than physical injury.
words.example: The rejection caused her deep hurt.

words.definitionEn: Payments into a public system that helps fund benefits and services in the UK.
words.example: His payslip showed his national insurance contributions.

words.definitionEn: The publicly funded healthcare system in the United Kingdom.
words.translationUz: Buyuk Britaniya Milliy sog'liqni saqlash xizmati (NHS)
words.example: She works for the NHS.

words.definitionEn: A fee paid for medicine supplied on prescription.
words.translationUz: retsept bo'yicha beriladigan dori uchun to'lov
words.example: The leaflet explained the prescription charge.

words.definitionEn: To identify an illness from symptoms, examination or tests.
words.example: The doctor used the results to diagnose the illness.

words.definitionEn: To identify a health problem without being physically with the patient.
words.example: The article considered whether doctors could diagnose from a distance.

words.definitionEn: Near the beginning of a process or condition.
words.example: The screening programme aims to detect disease at an early stage.

words.definitionEn: To provide care for a condition / to eliminate it or restore health.
words.example: A treatment may control symptoms without curing the disease.

words.definitionEn: To produce goods, usually on an industrial scale.
words.example: The company manufactures medical equipment.

words.definitionEn: To achieve progress quickly.
words.example: Researchers have made rapid advances in imaging technology.

words.definitionEn: A very large variety.
words.example: The exhibition displayed a vast range of medical devices.

words.definitionEn: Equipment that is advanced and complex.
words.example: The laboratory uses sophisticated equipment.

words.definitionEn: Working very effectively with little wasted time or effort.
words.example: The new system is highly efficient.

words.definitionEn: A large or sudden increase.
words.example: The report recorded a sharp rise in demand for appointments.

words.definitionEn: Health difficulties that continue or have effects for a long time.
words.example: The study examined long-term health problems.

words.term: To cause serious harm to the body
words.definitionEn: To produce significant physical damage.
words.example: The leaflet explained how tobacco can cause serious harm to the body.

words.definitionEn: Visit shops to buy things.
words.translationUz: xarid qilishga bormoq; do‘konma-do‘kon yurib xarid qilmoq
words.example: We plan to go shopping after work.

words.definitionEn: Buy the regular supplies a household needs.
words.translationUz: ro‘zg‘or uchun zarur mahsulotlarni xarid qilmoq
words.example: I usually do the shopping on Fridays.

words.definitionEn: Items produced or offered for sale.
words.example: The shop sells household goods.

words.definitionEn: Looking at items on display without intending to buy them.
words.translationUz: xarid qilmasdan vitrinalardagi mahsulotlarni tomosha qilish
words.example: We spent the afternoon window shopping.

words.definitionEn: Searching for products sold at particularly good prices.
words.translationUz: chegirmali yoki foydali narxdagi mahsulotlarni izlash
words.example: She enjoys bargain hunting at weekend markets.

words.definitionEn: Compare what different sellers offer before buying.
words.translationUz: xariddan oldin turli do‘konlardagi narx va sifatni solishtirmoq
words.example: It pays to shop around for a new washing machine.

words.definitionEn: Look through items casually without deciding to buy.
words.example: Customers can browse the displays at their own pace.

words.definitionEn: Put on clothing to check its fit or appearance.
words.example: May I try on this coat?

words.term: take something back / return an item
words.definitionEn: Bring or send a purchase back to the seller.
words.translationUz: xarid qilingan mahsulotni sotuvchiga qaytarib bermoq
words.example: I need to return an item that arrived damaged.

words.definitionEn: Replace a purchase with another item, such as a different size.
words.translationUz: xaridni boshqa mahsulotga yoki o‘lchamga almashtirmoq
words.example: Can I exchange this shirt for a larger one?

words.definitionEn: Available for someone to buy.
words.example: The paintings in the window are for sale.

words.definitionEn: A written record of items you intend to buy.
words.example: I added rice to my shopping list.

words.definitionEn: Buy goods through websites or apps.
words.translationUz: internet orqali xarid qilmoq; onlayn savdo
words.example: I prefer to shop online when I know exactly what I need.

words.definitionEn: Request a product to be supplied or delivered.
words.example: You can order the book from our website.

words.definitionEn: Obtain something by paying for it.
words.example: We decided to purchase a new sofa.

words.definitionEn: Someone visiting shops or looking for things to buy.
words.example: The shopper compared several jackets.

words.definitionEn: Someone who buys goods or services from a business.
words.example: The customer asked for a receipt.

words.definitionEn: A person or business selling goods directly to the public.
words.example: The retailer offers home delivery.

words.definitionEn: Someone who searches for unusually good deals.
words.translationUz: arzon va manfaatli takliflarni qidiradigan xaridor
words.example: A patient bargain hunter can find excellent furniture here.

words.definitionEn: An employee who helps customers in a shop.
words.example: The sales assistant found a different size for me.

words.definitionEn: The employee who handles customers' payments.
words.example: The cashier counted my change.

words.definitionEn: A person selling goods from a market stall.
words.translationUz: bozor savdogari; bozorda savdo qiluvchi sotuvchi
words.example: The market trader arranged fruit on the stall.

words.definitionEn: An employee who looks for and helps prevent theft in a shop.
words.translationUz: do‘konda o‘g‘rilikning oldini olishni nazorat qiluvchi xodim
words.example: The store detective watches for suspicious behaviour.

words.definitionEn: The help a business gives customers before, during and after a purchase.
words.translationUz: mijozlarga xizmat ko‘rsatish; mijozlarga yordam xizmati
words.example: Good customer service includes answering questions clearly.

words.definitionEn: Try persistently or forcefully to persuade someone to buy.
words.translationUz: mijozga kuchli bosim o‘tkazib mahsulot sotishga urinmoq
words.example: Some salespeople give customers the hard sell instead of listening.

words.definitionEn: Stealing goods from a shop while pretending to be a customer.
words.example: The shop introduced measures to reduce shoplifting.

words.definitionEn: A place where goods are sold to customers.
words.example: A new retail outlet opened near the station.

words.definitionEn: One shop in a group owned or operated by the same company.
words.translationUz: bir kompaniyaga tegishli savdo tarmog‘idagi do‘kon
words.example: The chain store stocks the same products in every branch.

words.definitionEn: A shop run separately from a large retail chain.
words.translationUz: katta savdo tarmog‘iga kirmaydigan mustaqil do‘kon
words.example: The independent store sells locally made gifts.

words.definitionEn: A large shop organised into sections selling different kinds of goods.
words.translationUz: turli bo‘limlarga ajratilgan yirik universal do‘kon
words.example: The department store has clothing upstairs and furniture downstairs.

words.definitionEn: A small local shop selling everyday essentials, often with long opening hours.
words.translationUz: kundalik zarur mahsulotlar sotiladigan kichik, odatda uzoq ishlaydigan do‘kon
words.example: The convenience store stays open late.

words.definitionEn: A large self-service shop selling food and household supplies.
words.translationUz: supermarket; yirik o‘ziga o‘zi xizmat ko‘rsatadigan do‘kon
words.example: The supermarket has a large fresh-food section.

words.definitionEn: A shop specialising in goods at relatively low prices.
words.example: We bought cleaning products at the discount store.

words.definitionEn: A shop selling food and other everyday household supplies.
words.translationUz: oziq-ovqat va kundalik ro‘zg‘or buyumlari do‘koni
words.example: There is a grocery store near our flat.

words.definitionEn: A seller of fresh fruit and vegetables.
words.example: The greengrocer recommended the seasonal pears.

words.definitionEn: A person who prepares and sells meat.
words.example: The butcher cut the meat into smaller pieces.

words.definitionEn: A place where bread, cakes or similar baked goods are made or sold.
words.translationUz: nonvoyxona; non va pishiriqlar sotiladigan joy
words.example: The bakery sells fresh rolls each morning.

words.definitionEn: A person who sells fish for eating.
words.example: The fishmonger prepared the fish for us.

words.definitionEn: A shop selling farm produce directly to customers.
words.example: The farm shop sells eggs and vegetables.

words.definitionEn: A shop that supplies medicines and may also sell toiletries and other goods.
words.example: I bought shampoo at the pharmacy.

words.definitionEn: A shop selling newspapers, magazines and often small everyday items.
words.example: The newsagent's sells newspapers and stationery.

words.definitionEn: A shop selling supplies for pets and sometimes animals.
words.translationUz: uy hayvonlari va ular uchun mahsulotlar do‘koni
words.example: The pet shop sells food for our rabbit.

words.definitionEn: A shop selling books.
words.example: The bookshop has a children's reading corner.

words.definitionEn: A shop selling materials and equipment for home improvement.
words.translationUz: uy ta’miri uchun jihoz va materiallar do‘koni
words.example: We bought paint at the DIY store.

words.definitionEn: A shop selling tools, fittings and items such as screws and nails.
words.translationUz: xo‘jalik asbob-uskunalari va mayda temir buyumlar do‘koni
words.example: The hardware shop stocks replacement handles.

words.definitionEn: A shop or counter selling prepared foods, cheeses and sliced meats.
words.translationUz: tayyor yeguliklar, pishloq va go‘sht mahsulotlari sotiladigan delikates do‘koni
words.example: We bought olives and cheese at the deli.

words.definitionEn: A place where traders sell goods from stalls.
words.example: The market is busiest on Saturdays.

words.definitionEn: A market selling second-hand goods and miscellaneous older items.
words.translationUz: eski va ikkinchi qo‘l buyumlar bozori
words.example: I found an old lamp at the flea market.

words.definitionEn: A building or planned group of buildings containing many shops.
words.example: The shopping centre has several entrances.

words.definitionEn: Prepaid credit given as a present and exchanged for goods or services.
words.translationUz: sovg‘a vaucheri; sovg‘a uchun xarid sertifikati
words.example: She gave me a gift voucher for the bookshop.

words.definitionEn: A document or code that reduces the amount payable on a purchase.
words.example: The discount voucher took ten pounds off my order.

words.definitionEn: A paper or digital token offering a discount or a free item.
words.translationUz: kupon; chegirma yoki bepul mahsulot olish huquqini beruvchi hujjat
words.example: The coupon entitled me to a free drink.

words.definitionEn: A retailer-linked credit card allowing purchases to be paid for later.
words.translationUz: muayyan do‘konda keyin to‘lash sharti bilan xarid qilish kartasi
words.example: He used his store card to pay for the furniture.

words.definitionEn: A card or account that records purchases to provide rewards or discounts.
words.translationUz: sodiqlik (bonus) kartasi; doimiy xaridorga imtiyoz beruvchi karta
words.example: I collected points on my loyalty card.

words.definitionEn: A payment card that uses money from the holder's bank account.
words.translationUz: debet karta; pulni bank hisobidan darhol yechadigan to‘lov kartasi
words.example: I paid for the groceries with my debit card.

words.definitionEn: A payment card that lets the holder borrow money and repay it later.
words.translationUz: kredit karta; qarz mablag‘i hisobidan to‘lov kartasi
words.example: She paid with a credit card and kept the receipt.

words.definitionEn: Money in the form of banknotes and coins.
words.example: The stall accepts cash.

words.definitionEn: A written or digital record showing that payment has been made.
words.example: Please email me the receipt.

words.definitionEn: Money returned to a customer after a payment.
words.example: The shop issued a refund for the damaged item.

words.definitionEn: The amount of money charged for something.
words.example: The price includes delivery.

words.definitionEn: A label showing how much an item costs.
words.example: The price tag was attached to the sleeve.

words.definitionEn: A reduction from the usual or stated price.
words.example: Students receive a discount on these notebooks.

words.definitionEn: A period or event when a seller reduces prices.
words.example: The shop is holding a sale this weekend.

words.definitionEn: Available at a reduced price in the promotional sense.
words.example: These towels are on offer until Sunday.

words.term: pick up a bargain / snap up a bargain
words.definitionEn: Buy something at a particularly favourable price.
words.translationUz: manfaatli narxdagi mahsulotni tezda yoki omad bilan xarid qilib olmoq
words.example: You can pick up a bargain at the end-of-season sale.

words.definitionEn: A price much lower than the usual amount.
words.example: They sold the display table at a knock-down price.

words.definitionEn: Reduce prices sharply.
words.example: The store plans to slash prices to clear old stock.

words.definitionEn: Costing a lot of money.
words.example: The leather bag was too expensive for me.

words.definitionEn: Not costing much money.
words.example: We found an inexpensive desk for the study.

words.definitionEn: Worth the amount paid because of the quality or usefulness received.
words.translationUz: to‘langan pulga yarasha sifat yoki foyda; narxiga arziydigan mahsulot
words.example: The durable shoes offer good value for money.

words.definitionEn: More expensive than its quality or usefulness justifies.
words.translationUz: haddan tashqari qimmat; asossiz yuqori narxli
words.example: The small souvenir seemed overpriced.

words.definitionEn: Gradually put money aside for a future purchase or purpose.
words.example: I need to save up for a new bicycle.

words.definitionEn: Negotiate with a seller about the price.
words.example: Some customers like to haggle at the market.

words.definitionEn: The point where a customer pays for purchases.
words.translationUz: kassa; xarid uchun to‘lov qilinadigan joy
words.example: Take your basket to the checkout.

words.definitionEn: A line of people waiting their turn; also, to wait in such a line.
words.example: There was a long queue near the till.

words.definitionEn: Flat horizontal surfaces used to display or store products.
words.example: The shelves were filled with breakfast cereal.

words.definitionEn: A wheeled container used to carry purchases around a shop.
words.translationUz: do‘konda mahsulot tashish uchun g‘ildirakli savat/aravacha
words.example: I put the heavy bags in the trolley.

words.definitionEn: A space where customers try on clothes.
words.example: There is a mirror in the fitting room.

words.definitionEn: The times during which a business is open to customers.
words.example: Check the opening hours before you travel.

words.definitionEn: The name and identity that distinguish a company's products from others.
words.translationUz: brend; mahsulotni boshqa ishlab chiqaruvchilardan ajratuvchi savdo belgisi
words.example: The brand is known for simple packaging.

words.definitionEn: Well-known brands recognised by many consumers.
words.example: The centre attracts several big brand names.

words.definitionEn: Products sold under a recognised commercial brand.
words.translationUz: mashhur savdo belgisi ostida chiqarilgan mahsulotlar
words.example: The shop stocks brand-name goods as well as cheaper alternatives.

words.definitionEn: Familiar retail brands commonly found in shopping streets, especially in Britain.
words.translationUz: Buyuk Britaniyaning savdo ko‘chalarida uchraydigan mashhur brendlar
words.example: The town has several well-known high street names.

words.definitionEn: Something desirable for comfort or pleasure rather than a necessity.
words.translationUz: hashamat; zarur bo‘lmagan, lekin yoqimli qimmatbaho buyum
words.example: For me, a handmade handbag is a luxury.

words.definitionEn: A possession valued because it signals wealth, success or social position.
words.translationUz: boylik yoki ijtimoiy mavqeni bildiruvchi ramz/buyum
words.example: Some people view a designer watch as a status symbol.

words.definitionEn: Previously owned or used by someone else.
words.example: We bought a second-hand dining table.

words.definitionEn: Not authentic; made to imitate something else.
words.example: The bag turned out to be a fake designer product.

words.definitionEn: Authentic and truly what it claims to be.

words.definitionEn: Major, established media outlets with large audiences (major TV networks, newspapers)

words.example: The course examines how new media change audience participation.

words.definitionEn: Established forms such as print newspapers, radio and scheduled television. Usage: Traditional media can also invite interaction or distribute content digitally.
words.translationUz: an’anaviy OAV; gazeta, radio va televideniye
words.example: The campaign used traditional media as well as online channels.

words.definitionEn: Information reflecting the most recent relevant developments. Usage: Also the latest information.
words.translationUz: eng so‘nggi o‘zgarishlarni aks ettiruvchi yangilangan ma’lumot
words.example: The website provides up-to-date information about the event.

words.definitionEn: The most recent news reports
words.example: I check my phone every morning for the latest news.

words.example: It's important to stay informed about current events.

words.definitionEn: To keep your knowledge current; to remain informed
words.example: Professionals need to stay up-to-date with industry developments.

words.example: The charity publicized the event through social media.

words.definitionEn: Determine what is actually true about a claim or event. Usage: More idiomatic for investigating than prove the truth behind; prove is suitable when demonstrating a specific claim.
words.translationUz: biror da’vo yoki hodisa ortidagi haqiqatni aniqlamoq

words.definitionEn: To learn about recent events globally that you may have missed
words.translationUz: dunyoda yuz bergan so‘nggi voqealardan xabardor bo‘lib olmoq
words.example: I read the news every morning to catch up with what's happening around the world.

words.definitionEn: A particular form or channel of communication. Usage: Plural: media. The collective media is represented by mass media elsewhere in this list.
words.translationUz: aloqa yoki axborot yetkazish vositasi; kanal

words.example: The film is on at eight tonight.

words.definitionEn: A question asking which programmes, shows or events are scheduled today. Usage: Can also refer to cinema or theatre listings. Straight apostrophes are also accepted.

words.definitionEn: A company or person that transmits television or radio programs

words.definitionEn: The people watching a programme or service, or the size of that audience.

words.definitionEn: A broadcast show on television
words.example: Educational TV programmes can inform while entertaining audiences.

words.definitionEn: A newspaper printed in a large-page format; the term is also associated with serious news reporting. Usage: Format alone does not guarantee accuracy or quality; some publications associated with the broadsheet tradition use smaller formats.

words.example: The library keeps copies of several broadsheet newspapers.

words.definitionEn: A compact-format newspaper, or one associated with a popular, often sensational reporting style. Usage: Page format and reporting style are different ideas; not every compact paper is sensationalist.
words.example: The tabloid used a large photograph on its front page.

words.definitionEn: A report about a recent event in the news
words.example: The corruption scandal became the biggest news story of the year.

words.definitionEn: Sensational, celebrity-focused style of reporting news
words.translationUz: shov-shuv va mashhurlar haqidagi xabarlarga yo‘naltirilgan jurnalistika
words.example: Tabloid journalism focuses more on scandals than serious issues.

words.definitionEn: The titles of news stories, usually in large print
words.example: The scandal dominated news headlines for weeks.

words.term: be relegated to the back pages
words.definitionEn: Be placed in a less prominent position towards the end of a newspaper. Usage: The back pages can also be prominent sports pages; their significance depends on the publication.
words.example: A serious story may be relegated to the back pages.

words.definitionEn: The first pages of a newspaper where the most important stories appear
words.example: The scandal appeared on the front pages of every major newspaper.

words.definitionEn: Very important or exciting news worthy of the newspaper's first page
words.example: The Prime Minister's resignation was front-page news everywhere.

words.definitionEn: To give an account of news or events; to cover a story
words.example: The journalist traveled to the conflict zone to report on the situation.

words.definitionEn: Newspapers, magazines and journalists considered collectively; sometimes news media more broadly.

words.definitionEn: A published work such as a newspaper or magazine, or the act of making material public. Usage: Both noun senses are covered in this single entry.

words.definitionEn: A person or company that produces and distributes books, newspapers, or magazines

words.term: be in the headlines / make the headlines
words.definitionEn: Be or become a prominent subject of news coverage. Usage: Be in the headlines describes the state; make the headlines describes attracting the coverage.
words.example: The discovery could make the headlines.

words.definitionEn: A person who investigates and writes news stories
words.example: Reporters must verify facts before publishing to maintain credibility.

words.definitionEn: The people reading a publication, or the size of that group.
words.example: The survey examined the magazine’s readership.

words.definitionEn: Communication publications produced in physical printed form, such as newspapers and magazines. Usage: Printed materials is broader and may include leaflets, forms and other items not normally called media.
words.example: The campaign used print media to reach local readers.

words.definitionEn: Digital versions of newspapers or magazines accessible via internet
words.example: Most publications now offer online editions alongside or instead of print versions.

words.definitionEn: Make something particularly noticeable or important in a presentation. Usage: No a before prominence in this expression.
words.translationUz: biror narsani ko‘zga ko‘rinarli qilib ajratib ko‘rsatmoq
words.example: Editors decide when to give something prominence on the front page.

words.definitionEn: To report on or provide news about an event
words.example: All major networks covered the incident with live broadcasts.

words.definitionEn: Media that can report news without government control or censorship
words.example: A free press is essential for democracy to function properly.

words.definitionEn: The practice of controlling or suppressing information, books, or media
words.translationUz: senzura; axborotni cheklash yoki nazorat qilish
words.example: Internet censorship prevents citizens from accessing certain websites.

words.definitionEn: To remove or block parts of books, films, or news considered inappropriate
words.example: The government tried to censor reports about the protests.

words.definitionEn: When information can move freely without restrictions or censorship
words.example: Democracy depends on the free flow of information.

words.definitionEn: Make previously hidden information known, especially in the case of expose, information about wrongdoing. Usage: Expose often stresses uncovering wrongdoing; reveal is broader.
words.example: The report helped expose the hidden payments.

words.definitionEn: A report that reveals shocking or secret information
words.translationUz: yashirin yoki shov-shuvli ma’lumotlarni fosh etuvchi material
words.example: The newspaper published an exposé on the politician's financial crimes.

words.definitionEn: Protect against harm; as a noun, a protective measure or provision. Usage: Both verb and noun senses are covered once.
words.example: New laws safeguard journalists from harassment.

words.definitionEn: A person who prepares content for publication and decides what to include
words.example: The editor decided which stories would appear on the front page.

words.definitionEn: Checking information for accuracy as part of an editorial process. Usage: More natural wording than the source phrase editor verification.
words.example: The article underwent editorial verification before publication.

words.definitionEn: The places or people where journalists get their information Usage: Source of information is broader; source of news overlaps in this context.
words.translationUz: yangilik manbalari; axborot beruvchi shaxs yoki joylar
words.example: Journalists should verify information from multiple news sources.

words.definitionEn: In-depth reporting that uncovers hidden information, often about wrongdoing
words.example: Investigative journalism exposed the corporate scandal.

words.definitionEn: To use someone or something unfairly for your own benefit
words.translationUz: o‘z manfaati uchun insofsiz foydalanmoq; ekspluatatsiya qilmoq
words.example: Tabloids exploit celebrities' private lives to sell newspapers.

words.definitionEn: Enter or interfere with someone’s space, activity or privacy in an unwelcome way. Usage: Also intrude into someone’s life.
words.translationUz: birovning shaxsiy hayoti yoki ishiga noo‘rin aralashmoq
words.example: Photographers should not intrude on private moments.

words.definitionEn: Interfere seriously and unwelcome with someone’s private life or information. Usage: Invade also has other meanings outside this context.
words.example: Publishing private messages may invade someone’s privacy.

words.definitionEn: To examine something carefully to find the truth
words.example: Reporters investigated the claims of corruption.

words.definitionEn: To check that something is true or accurate
words.example: Journalists must verify facts before publishing stories.

words.definitionEn: Formally begin an examination of an event, issue or allegation. Usage: Also launch an official inquiry. The matter being investigated follows into.
words.example: The authorities decided to launch an official investigation into the complaint.

words.definitionEn: Twisted or changed from the truth; not accurate
words.example: The tabloid published a distorted version of events.

words.definitionEn: Based on facts; accurate and truthful
words.example: The report was purely factual with no opinions included.

words.definitionEn: Providing useful information or knowledge
words.example: The documentary was both entertaining and informative.

words.definitionEn: Intruding on someone's privacy in an unwanted way
words.example: Paparazzi use invasive tactics to photograph celebrities.

words.definitionEn: Disturbing someone's privacy in an unwelcome way
words.example: The documentary crew was criticized for intrusive filming methods.

words.definitionEn: To be constantly watched or observed with no private moments
words.translationUz: umuman shaxsiy hayot daxlsizligiga ega bo‘lmaslik
words.example: Famous actors complain they have no privacy at all.

words.definitionEn: To form opinions without firm evidence; to conjecture
words.example: Media outlets speculate about politicians' motives without factual basis.

words.definitionEn: A famous person, especially in entertainment or sports
words.example: The restaurant is popular with celebrities and wealthy customers.

words.definitionEn: Known by many people. Usage: Famous does not automatically mean admired or morally good. Famous does not automatically mean admired.
words.example: The famous actor was recognised at the station.

words.definitionEn: Liked or enjoyed by many people. Usage: A person can be famous but unpopular.
words.example: The programme is popular with younger viewers.

words.definitionEn: A person with a publicly prominent role or identity. Usage: The expression itself does not define a universal legal rule about privacy.
words.example: As a public figure, she is often interviewed by journalists.

words.definitionEn: The state of being known by many people
words.example: He achieved international fame after winning the championship.

words.definitionEn: To present information in a way that makes it seem more exciting or shocking than it is Usage: American spelling: sensationalize.
words.example: The media tends to sensationalize minor incidents.

words.definitionEn: Conversation or reporting about other people’s personal lives. Usage: May be true, false or uncertain; it is not identical to rumour.
words.translationUz: g‘iybat; boshqalarning shaxsiy hayoti haqidagi gap-so‘zlar
words.example: The column mixes celebrity interviews with gossip.

words.definitionEn: A circulating claim whose truth has not been confirmed. Usage: American spelling: rumor. A rumour need not concern someone’s private life.
words.example: The reporter checked the rumour before mentioning it.

words.definitionEn: Say things about someone when they are absent, usually critically or unkindly. Usage: Also backbiting for unkind talk about an absent person.
words.example: She dislikes colleagues who talk behind someone’s back.

words.definitionEn: Intense or exaggerated publicity and promotion in the media. Usage: Not identical to sensation, which refers to strong excitement or something causing it.
words.example: The programme attracted considerable media hype.

words.definitionEn: Strong public excitement or interest, or something that causes it. Usage: Distinct from exaggerated publicity itself.
words.example: The unexpected announcement caused a sensation.

words.definitionEn: To deliberately seek attention and public recognition
words.translationUz: ataylab shuhrat va omma e’tiboriga intilmoq
words.example: Some reality TV stars court fame through controversial behavior.

words.definitionEn: Presenting information in an exaggerated, shocking way to attract attention
words.example: Sensationalist headlines often misrepresent the actual story.

words.definitionEn: Photographers who pursue celebrities for photographs, often intrusively. Usage: Plural; singular paparazzo.
words.example: The actor spoke about being followed by paparazzi.

words.definitionEn: To be well-known and constantly receiving public attention
words.example: Politicians are always in the public eye and must be careful about their behavior.

words.definitionEn: A person whose behavior is copied or admired by others
words.example: Athletes should remember they're role models for young people.

words.definitionEn: Widely known for something bad or discreditable. Usage: Infamous is not merely an emphatic form of famous.
words.translationUz: yomon ishlari bilan nom chiqargan; badnom
words.example: The incident became infamous because of the deception involved.

words.definitionEn: To become famous very quickly and suddenly
words.example: The young singer shot to fame after winning the talent competition.

words.definitionEn: Something that becomes extremely popular globally
words.translationUz: dunyo miqyosida mashhur hodisa; global fenomen
words.example: The K-pop group became a worldwide phenomenon, attracting millions of fans.

words.definitionEn: To become the focus of news coverage
words.example: Controversial statements attract media attention regardless of merit.

words.definitionEn: Attracting a lot of attention or publicity; prominent
words.example: High-profile cases receive extensive media coverage.

words.definitionEn: People who become famous very quickly, often through viral content
words.translationUz: bir zumda mashhur bo‘lib qolgan insonlar
words.example: Social media creates instant celebrities who may lack traditional talent or achievement.

words.definitionEn: Known throughout the world; internationally recognized
words.example: The world-famous actor commands millions per film.

words.definitionEn: To achieve fame very suddenly
words.translationUz: kutilmaganda bir kechada mashhur bo‘lib qolmoq
words.example: The internet allows people to become famous overnight through viral content.

words.definitionEn: Important and well-known; standing out
words.example: Prominent politicians receive constant media scrutiny.

words.definitionEn: Distinguished and respected in a particular field; renowned for achievement
words.translationUz: o‘z sohasida katta hurmatga sazovor; taniqli
words.example: The eminent scientist won numerous awards for groundbreaking research.

words.definitionEn: Newspaper or magazine sections featuring rumors and stories about celebrities' personal lives
words.example: Gossip columns thrive on scandal and speculation about famous people.

words.definitionEn: Recently acquired celebrity status
words.example: Many struggle to cope with new-found fame and its pressures.

words.definitionEn: The main reason someone is known or recognized
words.translationUz: kishining tanilishidagi asosiy sabab yoki yutug‘i
words.example: His chief claim to fame is appearing in one viral video.

words.definitionEn: To achieve recognition through effort, talent, or achievement
words.translationUz: mehnat yoki yutuq orqali shuhrat qozonmoq
words.example: True artists earn fame through dedication and skill over years.

words.term: feed an insatiable appetite for media attention
words.definitionEn: Continually supply publicity sought with a seemingly unlimited desire. Usage: Source uses the insatiable appetite. To describe audiences consuming stories, feed the public’s appetite for celebrity news is often clearer.
words.translationUz: ommaviy axborot vositalari e’tiboriga bo‘lgan cheksiz ehtiyojni tinimsiz qondirmoq
words.example: The publicity campaign seemed designed to feed an insatiable appetite for media attention.

words.term: increase the hype around a show
words.definitionEn: To build excitement and publicity for a program
words.example: Networks increase the hype around new shows through aggressive marketing campaigns.

words.definitionEn: Exceed reasonable or acceptable limits. Usage: Often followed by in doing something.
words.translationUz: me’yordan oshib ketmoq; haddan ortiq ketmoq
words.example: The reporter admitted that the questioning had begun to go too far.

words.definitionEn: Make excessive or unreasonable efforts to achieve something. Usage: Usually followed by to + verb.
words.translationUz: biror maqsad yo‘lida bema’ni darajada ko‘p urinish qilmoq
words.example: Some photographers go to ridiculous lengths to obtain a picture.

words.definitionEn: To provide content for celebrity news sections
words.example: Reality stars' scandals fill the gossip columns weekly.

words.definitionEn: Exaggerated or shocking titles designed to attract attention
words.example: Sensational headlines prioritize clicks over accuracy in online journalism.

words.definitionEn: When news coverage unfairly favors one perspective over others Usage: The PDF’s media prejudice is included here as a closely related formulation.
words.example: The newspaper was criticized for media bias in its political reporting.

words.definitionEn: To favor one political side unfairly in reporting or opinions
words.translationUz: siyosiy jihatdan tarafkash; bir siyosiy tomonni yoqlovchi
words.example: Many viewers believe news channels are politically biased.

words.definitionEn: To be done for political reasons or to gain political advantage Usage: Political motivation alone does not establish whether a claim is true or false.
words.translationUz: siyosiy sabab yoki manfaat bilan qilingan
words.example: The investigation was criticized as being politically motivated.

words.definitionEn: A tendency or preference that can unfairly affect judgement or presentation. Usage: Media bias applies the idea specifically to media presentation.
words.example: The editor checked the article for bias.

words.definitionEn: Reporting about an election without unfairly favouring one side. Usage: Also impartial coverage of the election. Both repeated source formulations are combined here.
words.example: The editor called for unbiased election coverage.

words.definitionEn: Unfairly favoring one side over another
words.example: The article was clearly biased against the opposition party.

words.definitionEn: Not unfairly favouring a person, side or viewpoint. Usage: Close equivalents here. Impartial does not require treating every unverified claim as equally credible.
words.example: The panel was asked to remain impartial.

words.definitionEn: A person seeking or being considered for a position or election
words.example: Presidential candidates face intense media scrutiny during campaigns.

words.definitionEn: Become involved in political activity or public political competition. Usage: The political arena is figurative, not a physical stadium.
words.example: She decided to enter the political arena.

words.definitionEn: To be officially chosen to run for a position
words.example: She hopes to be nominated as a candidate.

words.definitionEn: The ways media organisations report on and portray women. Usage: Women is generally more natural than females as a general noun for people in this context.
words.translationUz: matbuotning ayollarni qanday yoritishi va tasvirlashi
words.example: The study examines press treatment of women in sport.

words.definitionEn: People running for the position of president
words.example: Presidential candidates endure grueling campaigns under constant media observation.

words.definitionEn: Deal with a person in a just and reasonable way.
words.example: An interviewer should try to treat someone fairly.

words.definitionEn: Deal with a person in an unjust or unreasonable way.
words.example: A biased report can treat someone unfairly.

words.definitionEn: Hinder or slow advancement or development. Usage: Progress is usually uncountable; use the progress of a specified project if needed.
words.example: Lack of reliable information can impede progress.

words.term: take part in the political process
words.definitionEn: To participate in politics through voting, campaigning, or running for office
words.example: Citizens should take part in the political process to influence governance.

words.term: ascribe stereotypical traits to a group
words.definitionEn: Attribute oversimplified, generalised characteristics to a category of people. Usage: Natural clarification of ascribe stereotypes to some group. Also stereotype a group.
words.translationUz: biror guruhga stereotip xususiyatlarni nisbat bermoq
words.example: A misleading report may ascribe stereotypical traits to a group.

words.definitionEn: Represent a person in a particular way. Usage: Follow as with a noun or adjective.
words.translationUz: kimnidir muayyan shaxs yoki sifat sifatida tasvirlamoq
words.example: The report seemed to portray someone as a hero.

words.definitionEn: People in charge who lack the necessary skills or ability
words.example: The article criticised what it described as incompetent leaders.

words.definitionEn: Matters of public policy and governance
words.example: Coverage should focus on political issues rather than personalities.

words.definitionEn: Completely obvious and without shame; flagrant
words.example: Blatant media bias damages public trust in journalism.

words.definitionEn: To present something inaccurately or misleadingly
words.example: Selective editing can give a distorted view of an event.

words.definitionEn: Formal processes in which people choose representatives or decide positions by voting.
words.example: The broadcaster prepared its coverage of the elections.

words.definitionEn: To be contaminated or spoiled by something negative
words.translationUz: salbiy narsa bilan bulg‘angan; yomon ta’sir ostida qolgan
words.example: The account appeared to be tainted with personal prejudice.

words.definitionEn: Argue or maintain that a particular view is true. Usage: Often contend that + clause; not every use is interchangeable with assert.
words.translationUz: bir fikrni dalil sifatida ilgari surmoq; ta’kidlamoq
words.example: Critics contend that the comparison is misleading.

words.definitionEn: State something confidently or firmly. Usage: A confident assertion is not itself proof.
words.example: The spokesperson chose to assert that the report was accurate.

words.definitionEn: Influenced by personal feelings, judgements or perspective. Usage: Not automatically false or dishonest.
words.example: The review is a subjective response to the film.

words.definitionEn: Aiming to rely on evidence and minimise personal bias. Usage: Not a guarantee that a particular statement is correct.
words.example: The panel asked for an objective assessment.

words.definitionEn: The study of society, social relationships, and how people behave in groups
words.example: Her sociology class examined how media influences consumer behavior.

words.definitionEn: Take particular satisfaction in a quality, achievement or activity. Usage: Use pride oneself on, not pride oneself with. Change the reflexive pronoun as needed.
words.translationUz: o‘zining biror fazilati yoki yutug‘i bilan faxrlanmoq
words.example: The editor prides herself on checking sources carefully.

words.definitionEn: Ordinary people in society; everyone in general
words.example: The museum is now open to the general public after renovations.

words.definitionEn: To lack accurate or sufficient information about something
words.translationUz: yetarli yoki ishonchli ma’lumotga ega bo‘lmagan
words.example: Many people are ill-informed about climate change due to misleading news.

words.definitionEn: To gather and organize information to create a list
words.example: The magazine compiled a list of the top 100 influential people.

words.definitionEn: Using something as a reason or justification
words.translationUz: shunday degan asos bilan; shu sababga ko‘ra
words.example: The article was criticized on the basis that it contained false information.

words.definitionEn: When people copy others' actions because they assume those actions are correct
words.translationUz: ijtimoiy tasdiq; ko‘pchilik harakatini to‘g‘ri deb qabul qilish ta’siri
words.example: Social proof explains why people believe news stories shared by many others.

words.definitionEn: Influence from people in your social group to behave in certain ways
words.translationUz: tengdoshlar bosimi; ijtimoiy guruhdagi boshqalarning ta’siri
words.example: Teenagers often share fake news due to peer pressure on social media.

words.definitionEn: Topics that cause strong disagreement and debate
words.example: The newspaper avoided controversial issues to appeal to more readers.

words.definitionEn: What buyers want to purchase or receive
words.example: Tabloids exist because there's consumer demand for celebrity gossip.

words.definitionEn: Affect how someone thinks or how something develops. Usage: Also be an influence on someone.
words.example: Media reports can have an influence on public discussion.

words.definitionEn: To affect or change how someone thinks or how something happens
words.example: Advertisements influence consumers' purchasing decisions.

words.definitionEn: To cause a change in something or someone
words.translationUz: ta’sir qilmoq; biror o‘zgarishga sabab bo‘lmoq
words.example: Negative news coverage can affect public opinion.

words.definitionEn: Produce a change or consequence for someone or something. Usage: Affect is usually a verb; effect here is a noun.
words.example: The announcement may have an effect on viewing figures.

words.definitionEn: Not natural or genuine; made or produced by humans
words.example: The documentary's dialogue felt artificial and scripted.

words.definitionEn: Spreading widely; existing everywhere
words.translationUz: juda keng tarqalgan; hamma joyda mavjud
words.example: Media influence is pervasive in modern society.

words.definitionEn: Dealing only with surface-level aspects; lacking depth
words.example: The news coverage was superficial and didn't explain the real issues.

words.definitionEn: To attract and hold someone's interest
words.example: Shocking headlines grab attention but may sacrifice accuracy.

words.definitionEn: Designed to attract notice; eye-catching
words.example: Tabloids use attention-grabbing headlines to increase sales.

words.definitionEn: To reconsider or think about something again
words.example: The editor may need to rethink something after hearing new evidence.
